info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

get.summary: Lists the actions this caller may invoke.
get.description:
Filtered by license, privilege, and the kill-switch — the same conditions
the gate applies to an invocation. A tool a caller can see but not invoke
wastes a turn for a model and misleads a human, so the list and the gate
must not disagree.

post.summary: Invokes an action as the calling human.
post.description:
There is no way to invoke as anything else: `ActionContext::user` takes the
caller's own `SecurityContext` and there is no service-principal overload
(I-3). The agent path — which supplies a risk ceiling and a taint flag —
arrives with agent sessions (TODO-039) and goes through the same
`dispatch`.

x-audit-exempt.note: the mandatory Ai+Execute event `dispatch` writes is agent-attribution-gated (ctx.is_agent(), C19/D-541 rule 4) and this route always invokes as the plain calling human (ActionContext::user, see this fn's own doc comment) — never an agent session — so that write never fires here; whatever the invoked action itself mutates is audited by that action's own executor (e.g. a record write goes through entity_crud)

`POST /api/v1/admin/approval-policies` — `system.admin` only. `plan` is

shape (`attome_audit::approval::validate_plan_approvers`) before insert.

for `action_type` — the partial unique index migration `0183` enforces.

evaluated: there is still at most one candidate policy to check a

`find_matching_policy`'s doc comment).

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/admin/approvals` — `system.admin` only. Lists requests,
newest-first, optionally filtered to one `action_type` and to one or more
`status` values (default `pending`).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Comma-separated status filter, in the request's own vocabulary
(`pending`, `approved`, `executing`, `rejected`, `expired`,
`executed`, `cancelled`, `invalidated`). Defaults to `pending` —
today's behavior. BAP-10: `approved` and `executing` are how an
operator finds an approved-but-unexecuted action and a claim whose
holder died; neither was listable before. An unknown name is `422`.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/admin/approvals/batch-decide` — decide many requests the
same way (roadmap N30-T6). Each is decided on its own through the exact
path a single decision takes ([`do_decide`]): its own row-version check,
separation of duties, transaction, audit events and, for an approval
that closes it, execution. One failing never stops the others; the
response says what happened to each.

422.description: Unknown decision, no items, more than 100, or a comment too long

x-audit-exempt.note: each request is decided through the single-decision path, which writes its own Approved/Rejected event and decision digest in its own transaction

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/admin/approvals/{id}` — `system.admin` reads any request;
the fleet console's rollout credential (`metadata.rollout`, D-792) reads
only a request it submitted itself (the `metadata.changeset_apply`
request its apply opened), so the console can follow it. Another
principal's request is `404`, never `403`, so the route does not confirm
that a request id exists. Read-only: no route that decides, cancels,
retries or delegates accepts the rollout credential.

404.description: No such request, or (rollout credential) a request it did not submit

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/admin/approvals/{id}/cancel` — `system.admin` only, and
further restricted to the request's own `requested_by` by
`attome_approval::cancel` itself (`Forbidden` otherwise) — the inverse of
`decide()`'s separation-of-duties check. Lets an admin withdraw a request
they no longer want decided (submitted in error, superseded, etc.)
without waiting out the full `approval.ttl_hours` for it to expire.

`POST /api/v1/admin/approvals/{id}/decide` — `system.admin` only.
`attome_approval::decide` enforces the separation-of-duties invariant
(`ctx.user_id` cannot be the request's own `requested_by`) and the
`row_version` CAS; see that function's doc comment. On `Approve` closing
the request (today's callers all use `required_approvals = 1`, so a
single approval always closes it), this call also executes the approved
action inline and returns its result in `executed` — the client does not
need a second call.

409.description: Stale row_version, or the request is already decided, expired, or being decided

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/admin/approvals/{id}/delegate` — `system.admin` only, D-421
/ M10. Lets `ctx.user_id` (who must actually be one of the *named*
approvers on this request's current plan step — `create_request_delegation`
checks that, `Forbidden` otherwise) hand their standing on this request's
`action_type` to another user, for the rest of this request's window
unless `valid_to` narrows it. Only valid on a plan-bearing (policy-driven)
request — the original flat `required_approvals` model has no per-step
eligibility to delegate.

`POST /api/v1/admin/approvals/{id}/retry-execution` — `system.admin`
only. Recovery path for the gap `decide_approval` above has no answer
for: if execution fails AFTER `attome_approval::decide` already committed
`status = 'approved'`, the request could never be re-decided (`decide()`
only ever accepts a `Pending` request) and, before this endpoint existed,
had no way back to `executed` either — a permanently stuck
four-eyes-approved action.
post.description:
**One execution per approval (D-518).** This claims the request
(`approved -> executing`) before running anything, as `decide_approval`
does, so two retries, or a retry racing the deciding call, never both run
the action; the loser gets `409`. By state:
- `approved` with no `executed_at`: claim, then run.
- `executing` inside the claim lease: `409`, another call is running it.
- `executing` past the lease: the earlier attempt died or hung, or its
  close-out failed, and whether its action ran is unknown. `409` unless
  `acknowledge_unknown_outcome=true`, which an admin passes only after
  checking the action's effect; the takeover is audited before the action
  runs again.
- anything else: `409`.

**Known limitation.** An executor error releases the claim, so a retry
re-runs that `do_*` from scratch. That is safe for a `do_*` that failed
outright (a transient DB/network error, so nothing was applied), not for
one that partially applied its effect and then failed. None of the
action_types wired today are known to do this (each is a single bounded
write or a single job-enqueue), but that has not been verified per
action_type.

Uses the retrying admin's own identity as `approver_id` for whatever the
executed action attributes it to (see `dispatch_approved`'s doc comment)
— the original approving admin's decision is already the `Approved`
audit event `decide_approval` wrote; this call's own audit event below
records who actually caused execution to run.

parameters.name: acknowledge_unknown_outcome
parameters.description:
D-518 — only for a request whose earlier execution attempt passed its
claim lease without finishing, so whether its action ran is unknown.
Pass `true` after checking the action's effect: the action runs again,
and the takeover is audited. Ignored in every other state.

409.description: The request is not stuck approved, another call is executing it, or an unknown outcome was not acknowledged

post.summary:
AG1-T6: a holiday that falls on the same Hijri date every year (Eid
al-Fitr is 1 Shawwal), entered once: one holiday per Hijri year from
`from_year` to `to_year` (at most 30 years), each on its Gregorian day
in the deployment's Umm al-Qura calendar, all in one transaction. A 30th
in a year whose month has 29 days falls on the next day, the 1st of the
following month, as announced holidays do. Refused whole when any day
already has a holiday or an exception.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/admin/changes` — `system.admin` only. Unifies the metadata
change log, the bundle apply ledger, every `_version`/publish-style change
this deployment tracks, security grant changes, AI model-registry
changes, and runtime settings changes into one ordered, filterable feed,
paged by an opaque keyset cursor. See the module doc for exactly what each
`kind` reads, the total order, and why the envelope is the keyset
`CursorPage<T>`, not `PaginatedResponse<T>`.

delete.summary:
Solution 7 Phase 2 (D-788 rules 4 and 9): a **real delete**. The
field's non-null values are copied to the encrypted 30-day recovery
archive, its references are removed (ours must already be gone — they
block, listed; customer objects are adjusted and reported), the column is
dropped and the attribute row deleted, in one transaction (above the
size gate the archive copy runs as a batched run: `202` with `run_id`).
`?dry_run=true` returns the archive count, the references and the
blockers without writing. Recorded as `delete_field`. Gated like every
schema change (`schema.attribute_change`).

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description:
Report what the change would do (counts, references, blockers)
without writing.

place**, same name. Values that do not convert become empty (even for a
required field — required is application-level), are copied to the
encrypted 30-day recovery archive, and are reported. At or under the size
gate one transaction; above it a shadow column with a sync trigger is
backfilled in batches and swapped (`202` with `run_id`). Runs without
business rules or workflows. `dry_run` returns the `not_convertible`
count and sample record ids. Recorded as `change_field_type`.

post.summary:
Solution 7 Phase 2 (D-788 rule 3): renames the field **in place** — the
column (`ALTER TABLE … RENAME COLUMN`, no data moved), its index and
CHECK names, the attribute row, and every reference through the hook
registry (views, stored queries, forms, labels, rules, state models,
workflows, field security, lineage; customer objects adjusted and
reported), in one transaction. No alias: API integrations using the old
name break (reported as a breaking change). A reference of ours that
cannot be rewritten safely blocks it (409 `rename_blocked_by_reference`,
listed). Recorded as `rename_field`.

409.description: Blocked by references (listed), the new name exists, the field is busy, or another open changeset touches the entity

post.summary:
Solution 7 Phase 2 (D-788): abandons a **failed** batched run of a field
change (a large type change, `retype`; a large delete's archive copy,
`archive`) so the field is no longer `field_busy`. One transaction: the
field and the run are locked; a retype's shadow column, sync trigger and
trigger function are dropped; the run's recovery-archive rows are removed
(nothing was destroyed: the column still holds every value); the run is
marked `abandoned` with its cursor cleared. A retype whose swap had
already committed is closed without undoing anything
(`conversion_completed`). A queued or running run is refused (409
`run_not_failed`). Not approval-gated: it only undoes the partial state of
a change that was gated when it started. The change's changeset op is not
removed (reported in `labels`).

404.description: No such run for this field

409.description: `run_not_failed`, or the table is busy (`field_busy`, retry)

get.summary:
P-online-schema-change §4(d). Deliberately reads its own dedicated
ledger row rather than deriving state the way `attribute_index_status`
derives from `pg_stat_progress_create_index`/`pg_index` above: there is
no Postgres system view analogous to that for a generic `ALTER TABLE`/
`VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`, and the backfill phase's per-batch progress
(`backfill_cursor`) has nowhere else to live. This is not a second copy
of catalog truth (the objection `index-status`'s own no-shadow-column
design correctly avoided, D-083) — it is the only place this information
exists at all.

automates exactly that manual procedure for a *named* bundle
([`super::model::Bundle::name`]/[`super::model::Bundle::version`]):
post.description:
1. find the newest `succeeded` ledger row for `name` whose stored bundle
   declares `version == to_version` (404 if none — either the name was
   never applied, or never at that version);
2. plan that stored snapshot against *current* live metadata, through the
   same [`plan_and_persist`] every `import?mode=plan` call uses (so a
   rollback plan is reviewable exactly like any other plan, and is
   persisted as its own ledger row — never a hidden, unaudited apply);
3. queue it through [`apply_with_gate`] — the same D-195 approval gate
   `import?mode=apply` and [`super::pull::sync`] use, so a production
   deployment still needs a second `system.admin` to approve
   (`ACTION_BUNDLE_APPLY`). This is the documented manual procedure,
   automated — never a bypass of the ordinary plan/apply/approval gates.

pattern `fetch_current_entity_mappings` already uses — a query whose
*current* published version no longer references `relation` (it was
edited to remove that join) correctly stops appearing here, even though an
older, superseded version once did; that's the right answer for "would
altering `relation` break something live today," not an audit-history
question.

`POST /api/v1/admin/relationships` — `system.admin` only. Creates the
relationship definition AND provisions its physical join table
(`mm_{name}`) — see `reconcile_relationship`'s doc comment for the
create-before-insert ordering and its failure-mode reasoning.
post.description:
**`name` is not renameable, and reusing a retired one after swapping
`entity_a`/`entity_b` is a `409` (C-21, M01 §7).** There is no
in-place rename endpoint: `join_table` is derived from `name` once, at
create time. Retiring one `name` and creating another under a different
`name` (the only way to get a differently-named relationship between the
same two entities) provisions a brand-new, empty `mm_{new name}`
table — it does not move data out of the old one, which stays exactly as
the retired relationship left it (`retire_relationship`'s doc comment).
Reusing the OLD `name` later is fine as long as `entity_a`/`entity_b`
match what it originally provisioned; if they don't, this endpoint
refuses with `409` rather than silently attaching the new relationship to
the old, wrongly-shaped physical table
(`attome_metadata::provision::relationship::verify_join_table_matches_or_absent`).

relationship's `/related/{relationship}` route immediately 404s (the
registry no longer resolves the name) even though the join rows survive
physically, in case the name is ever reused.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/admin/security/erasure/{logicalname}/{record_id}` —
`system.admin` only. Destroys `record_id`'s crypto-shredding key (if one
exists) and appends one audit event (`AuditOperation::Erasure`, no
`changed_fields`) recording that the erasure happened, by whom, and when
— through the same hash-chained `AuditService` path as every other audit
event, so the erasure action itself is exactly as tamper-evident as
anything else in the ledger.
post.description:
Idempotent: erasing an already-erased (or never-protected) record returns
200 with `key_destroyed: false/true` reflecting what THIS call actually
changed, never an error — a retried erasure request must not fail.

D-195: gated behind `approval.required_actions` (empty/off by default,
same opt-in shape as every other wired action). When gated, submits an
approval request for `{logicalname, record_id}` instead of destroying
anything and returns `202` with `approval_pending: true` — see this
module's doc comment for why a pending erasure request is exactly as
reversible as any other despite the underlying action's own
irreversibility.

post.summary:
Mints an invitation and, when this deployment has email configured,
enqueues it (`EngineJob::SendEmail`, never sent on the request path —
guidelines §10) in the same transaction as the token insert — same
commit-together discipline as `register`/`reset_request`, so an enqueue
failure rolls back the invitation instead of being logged and reported as
success (previously it was caught and only `tracing::warn!`-ed here).
Does not check whether `email` already has a live `user_account` row —
an admin re-inviting an existing user is treated as their call, not this
endpoint's to second-guess; `register` itself still rejects a
duplicate/disabled email at INSERT time regardless of whether the
invitation token validated.

state to add to `register`'s undifferentiated-403 reasoning, D-128 §8).

post.summary:
Creates (or reactivates) a share/deny row on one record. Never touches
the implicit creator-share — that row is written only by
`entity_crud::create_record`, with `principal_id` fixed to the caller
who made the record; this endpoint is for every OTHER grant (F137
sharing, deny).

put.summary:
D-137: reassigns a record's denormalized `owner_ref`/`owner_type` columns
(`attome_metadata::provision::provision_table`'s generic column set — never
consulted by `rls_predicate`, see `attome_core::sql_ident::ALL_SYSTEM_COLS`'s
doc comment) and ensures the new owner holds an `action`-capability
`record_share` row, so reassignment also grants access — matching
D365's "Assign" semantics — in one transaction. Deliberately does NOT
touch the previous owner's existing share row: D-133 (2) already treats a
deactivated/former owner's leftover share as a `Team+` actor's manual
cleanup concern, not an automatic cascade, and this endpoint carries that
same posture forward rather than inventing a second policy for it.
put.description:
admin-gated for now, the same scope boundary every other `record-shares`
mutation in this file already has — opening this to a non-admin caller who
merely holds `BusinessUnit+`/`Team+` `update` access on their own team's
records would need a dedicated `{entity}.share` privilege verb that does
not exist yet in the seeded four (`read`/`create`/`update`/`delete`).
Named here as a deliberate boundary, not a silently dropped requirement.

post.summary:

doc for what each covers). Advisory-locked per domain (guidelines §2 Layer 2)
so a second trigger while one is still running is rejected with `Conflict`
rather than enqueuing a redundant concurrent pass.

Assigns `role_id` to every member of `team_id` — the D-133 "everyone on
Finance team gets Finance Role" association. Distinct from
`role_grants::create_role_grant` (role → privilege); this is role → team.

client reliably sends as `application/json` for a POST with no other
fields (a bare string body serializes as `text/plain` by default in most
HTTP clients, which axum's `Json` extractor rejects).

dead-letter list) — `page` is one-based: page 1 is the first page.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/ai/conversations/{id}/stream` — the conversation's semantic
events as Server-Sent Events: every stored event after the cursor, in
ordinal order, then new ones as they commit (C10-A, I-14, row A-12).
get.description:
**Authorized before the first frame (I-20).** The conversation is resolved
for the caller before the response starts: an unknown conversation, or
someone else's, is an ordinary `404` with no stream.

**A projection of the log.** Every frame with an `id` is a committed event.
Replay and live-follow are one loop over `ordinal > cursor`, and a
conversation's events commit in ordinal order, so the handoff from replay
to live neither skips nor repeats one.

**Token deltas (C11 B3).** While following live, the stream also relays
`message.delta` frames — `{turn_id, text}`, **with no `id`**, so a delta
never moves the client's `Last-Event-ID` and a reconnect replays durable
events only (I-14, A-78). A delta for a turn whose `message.completed`
this stream has already sent is dropped: the answer supersedes it (A-79).
When Redis is unavailable there are no deltas and nothing else changes.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
Replay events with an ordinal greater than this (exclusive). Absent:
the `Last-Event-ID` header, else `0` — the whole log.

get.summary:
P-frontend-baseline step 5 (D-071/D-073) — public directory endpoint so the
login page can fetch the Google client id at runtime instead of it being
duplicated as a hardcoded literal in `environment.ts`. Falls under the
`/api/v1/auth/google` bypass entry already in force for `google_login`
(prefix match — no bypass-list change needed). Empty config string maps to
`None`, same "render no button" handling as an empty OIDC directory.

P-federation-linking-policy §4.3(a) callback — bypass-listed
(`attome_server::middleware::bypass`'s `/api/v1/auth/identity-link-callback/`
subtree prefix). This route deliberately does NOT require
`Extension<SessionClaims>`, even though it only ever does anything useful
for a caller who was logged in a moment ago: session cookies here are
`SameSite=Strict` (`attome_auth::cookie::build`), so the browser never
re-attaches one on this cross-site redirect back from the IdP — the
target user comes entirely from `OidcIdentity::linking_user_id`, resolved
server-side from the single-use state `identity_link_oidc_start` stashed
before redirecting to the IdP. Same failure-redirect shape as
`oidc_callback` (P2.8 step 5 precedent).

post.summary:
P-federation-linking-policy §4.3(a) extended to Google — analog of
`identity_link_oidc_start`, but Google's
credential flow is a single synchronous POST from the Google Identity
Services SDK (no authorization-code redirect), so there's no separate
start/callback pair to wire: one protected endpoint suffices. Session-gated
(`Extension<SessionClaims>`), deliberately NOT under the
`/api/v1/auth/google` bypass prefix `google_login`/`google_config` use
(guidelines §3: a bypass prefix must never also match a protected route)
— mounted at `/api/v1/auth/identity-link/google` instead, alongside the
OIDC start routes, for the same reason.

P-federation-linking-policy §4.3(a) UI support — self-scoped read of the
caller's own linked federated identities, backing the `/settings/security`
page's "already linked" state so it doesn't have to blindly offer every
configured OIDC provider as unlinked. `claims.sub` is always the
caller's own id (never a path/query parameter), so no additional
authorization check is needed beyond the ordinary `AuthnLayer`/`AuthzLayer`
this protected route already rides.

post.summary:
P2.8 step 7 (D-069): a correct password no longer always mints a session —
see `accounts::LoginOutcome`. The `MfaRequired`/`MfaEnrollmentRequired`
branches respond 200 with a `pending_token` instead of `Set-Cookie`; the
client must complete the flow via `/mfa/verify`, `/mfa/recovery`, or
`/mfa/pending-enroll` + `/mfa/pending-confirm` before a session exists.

Invalidates the presented session server-side (Plan 1.6a): denylists the
access token's `jti` for its remaining lifetime and revokes the refresh
token row, then clears both cookies. Malformed/absent/already-expired
tokens are not an error — logout always succeeds.

Disables the caller's MFA. The TOTP or recovery code in the request is this
request's step-up (D-510 rule 8): it is verified once, satisfies freshness
for this request only, and writes no elevation. Only a cookie session with
a live refresh family may call it (rule 7).

401.description: Missing or invalid credentials, a session without a live refresh family, or a missing, wrong or replayed code

403.description: An API-key or S2S caller: only a cookie session may disable MFA

429.description: Too many second-factor attempts for this account

post.summary:
Starts (or restarts) enrollment. Gated on `auth.mfa_policy != "off"` —
a deployment kill switch means no one can enroll, not just that login
stops requiring it (mirrors `reset_request`'s `email.enabled` gate).

Confirms forced enrollment and, on success, issues a real session
immediately (the `mfa_policy = "required"` first-login path completes in
one round trip: enroll, confirm, done) — plus the one-time-viewable
recovery-code batch in the response body alongside the cookies.

Starts forced enrollment (`mfa_policy = "required"`, account not yet
enrolled) using the `MfaEnrollmentRequired` pending token in place of a
session. Bypass-listed for the same reason as `mfa_verify`.

Regenerates the caller's recovery codes. The TOTP code in the request is
this request's step-up (D-510 rule 8): it is verified once, satisfies
freshness for this request only, and writes no elevation. Only TOTP is
accepted here (I11). Only a cookie session with a live refresh family may
call it (rule 7).

403.description: An API-key or S2S caller: only a cookie session may regenerate recovery codes

Whether the caller's own account has a confirmed TOTP enrollment — the

post.summary:
Completes an `MfaRequired` login with a TOTP code. Bypass-listed — the
caller has no session cookie yet (that's the whole point); identity comes
from `pending_token`, a short-lived, purpose-scoped token distinct from
`SessionClaims` (`attome_auth::mfa`), not from `AuthnLayer`.

Same as `mfa_verify` but via a single-use recovery code instead of a live
TOTP code.

get.summary:
P2.8 step 5 — public directory of configured OIDC providers so the Angular
login page can render provider buttons without duplicating provider keys/
labels in frontend config (killing the hardcoded-client-id pattern that
`google_login` still has). Falls under the `/api/v1/auth/oidc/` bypass
prefix already in force for the login/callback routes — no bypass-list
change needed. Never serializes `issuer`/`client_id`/`client_secret`/
`scopes`/`email_claim` — see `OidcProviderInfo`.

P2.8 (D-065) — the IdP redirects the browser back here with `code`+`state`.
Exchanges the code, verifies the ID token (signature/aud/iss/nonce —
`attome_auth::oidc::complete_login`), JIT-links the account
(`attome_security::accounts::link_oidc_identity`), issues the same session
cookies every other login path issues, and redirects to the frontend —
this is a top-level browser navigation from the IdP, not a fetch/XHR call,
so a redirect (not JSON) is the only response an IdP's redirect can
consume. Bypass-listed, same reasoning as `/refresh`.
get.description:
P2.8 step 5: any failure also redirects (to `{frontend_url}/login?oidc_error=1`)
rather than returning the raw `AppError` JSON body — a JSON blob mid IdP-redirect
isn't actionable for a browser user, and the `AppError` detail (e.g. exactly which
claim/state check failed) isn't for the client anyway (see §6). The real reason is
logged server-side, same as any other recoverable anomaly.

The provider's error code (`access_denied`, `consent_required`, …).

a config-driven provider (`config.oidc.providers.{provider}`). Redirects

P-session-refresh-hardening (D-129): `refresh::redeem` (not the old
`validate`) marks the presented token used and returns a replacement in
the same rotation family — reusing an already-redeemed token now revokes
the whole family instead of being silently accepted. Both cookies are
reissued together, closing the prior gap where only the access-token
cookie was refreshed and the same refresh cookie stayed live indefinitely.

post.summary:
P-registration-gating (D-128): `auth.registration_mode` gates this before
any DB work — `"disabled"` (the default) rejects outright, `"invite"`
requires a valid `invitation_token` matching `body.email`
(`accounts::register` validates and consumes it), `"public"` is today's
unconditional behavior. The route itself stays mounted and bypass-listed
(guidelines §3: the bypass list is a compile-time constant, not a runtime
toggle) — gating lives entirely in this handler.

post.summary:
Confirms a presented reset token. `reset::confirm` applies the whole reset
in one transaction (D-509): it consumes the token, sets the new password,
expires the account's other reset links, revokes every refresh token the
account holds and bumps `auth_epoch`, so live access tokens stop working
too. API keys and MFA enrollment are not touched.

Always responds 200 regardless of whether `body.email` matched an account
(anti-enumeration, guidelines/P-account-lifecycle) — only a match actually
enqueues an email. Bypass-listed, IP-rate-limited (this route classifies
as the `password_reset` category, `attome_server::middleware::rate_limit::
RATE_LIMIT_CATEGORIES` — its own independent, tighter budget, see
config.example.json).

(P-session-refresh-hardening, D-129) — bootstraps from this call at app

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/consents/capture` — the platform's public, anonymous
consent-capture entry point for a customer's own web forms (a newsletter
signup checkbox, a cookie-preferences banner, …). Registered as an exact
`attome_server::middleware::bypass::EXACT_BYPASS_PATHS` entry, so it skips
authn/authz the same way `/api/v1/content/view` and
`/api/v1/service-portal/offerings` do.
post.description:
CSRF is a non-issue here by construction, not by exemption: this route
never reads a session cookie (there is no `SecurityContext` for it to
act on), and the session/refresh cookies are `SameSite=Strict`
(`attome_auth::cookie::build`), so a browser never attaches either one to
a cross-site request in the first place — the same reasoning
`middleware::csrf::csrf_protect`'s own doc comment gives for every other
bypass-listed, non-session-acting route. It is therefore *not* added to
`CSRF_ENFORCED_BYPASS_PATHS` (that list is for the opposite case: a
bypass route that DOES act on a live cookie, e.g. logout/refresh).

Rate-limited like every other route (`middleware::rate_limit::rate_limit`
runs regardless of the bypass list) — see
`RATE_LIMIT_CATEGORIES`'s `consent_capture` entry — and additionally
covered by the coarse, pre-authn `pre_auth_rate_limit` IP backstop that
wraps the whole app before any body is read (`attome_server::app`), so an
abusive caller is throttled before this handler, or even the JSON body
extractor, ever runs.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/consents/withdraw` — inserts the withdrawal row (D-428:
always append, never update the row that recorded the grant). Does not
require an existing `granted` row to exist first: the caller is
asserting "this subject's consent for this purpose is withdrawn as of
now," which is meaningful evidence to keep even if the platform never
recorded a prior grant (e.g. a subject withdrawing consent that was
captured somewhere the platform doesn't know about).
post.description:
Policy: no `{entity}` path segment for `RecordScoped<A>` to authorize
against (guidelines §7 / `attome_server::authz`'s own doc comment), so this
is bare `RecordScoped` (declaration only) plus the hand-written
`ctx.require("audit_consent", "create")` — the same shape
`attome-api::bulk::enqueue` uses for a verb the extractor cannot see.

D-100: approving a staged import is enqueued, not run on the request
thread. The original synchronous handler ran one full transaction per
record inline in the HTTP response path with no size bound beyond the
original submission's `MAX_BULK_RECORDS` cap — a large approved import
could exceed `config.request_timeout` mid-loop, leaving the row stuck at
`status = 'approving'` forever (the `WHERE status = 'pending_review'`
guard on this same query meant a stuck row could never be re-approved or
retried). This handler now only validates, transitions the row, seeds the
item ledger, and enqueues — mirroring `enqueue`'s shape for regular bulk.

insert vs. update, the write itself goes through the same

the file-upload trust anchor (`lock_file_field_sessions`),

rather than inside one shared SQL statement.

means "page 1 of 1, everything returned": `total` is the actual row count

bigger, undesired change (a `page_size` with no way to request page 2).

(F026 restore can bring a dependent back later; it must not wake up
still pointing at a retired id). All three steps commit atomically â€”
a partially-redirected merge would be worse than the duplicate data it's
meant to fix.

`GET /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/related/{relationship}` — every live record on
the relationship's other side currently linked (through a live join row)
to the anchor record, paginated. Both endpoints' `is_active` and the
join row's own `is_active` are filtered — this is what makes
"soft-deleting either side hides the link" true unconditionally,
independent of the relationship's `cascade` policy (metadata-only in
this phase — see `RelationshipCascade`'s doc comment).

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/related/{relationship}` — links the anchor
record to `body.id` on the relationship's other side. Idempotent
upsert-by-natural-key (`ON CONFLICT (a_id, b_id) DO UPDATE`): linking an
already-linked pair is a no-op that also reactivates a previously
unlinked (soft-deleted) join row, rather than erroring.
post.description:
Requires `update` privilege AND record-level access on BOTH sides —
linking two records is a mutation on both of them, same reasoning
`guard_cascade_dependent_access` already applies to a cross-entity
cascade delete.

C-09 (M01 §7) gives this a real audit header + change-feed rows +
rw-pin (see the body). It does NOT stamp `modified_by`/`modified_at` on
the `DO UPDATE` reactivation branch below, as that item's text also
asks for: `attome_metadata::provision::relationship::provision_join_table`'s
`CREATE TABLE` never gave the join-table schema those two columns (only
`a_id`/`b_id`/`is_active`/`created_at`/`created_by`/`row_version`) — every
already-provisioned `mm_*` table in every deployment is missing
them too. Adding them is a real (if small) schema-evolution change in
`attome-metadata`, outside this fix's file scope; flagged here rather than
silently worked around.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/related/{relationship}?id=...` — unlinks
`?id=` from the anchor record (soft-deletes the join row: `is_active =
false`). A query parameter, not a JSON body: `DELETE` requests
conventionally carry no body, and `@attome/base`'s `ApiService.delete`
has never needed to send one — adding that capability there for this one
caller was worse than the alternative of a query-string identifier,
which every other id-bearing `DELETE` in this platform's contract
already carries in the path instead (this one can't, since the id names
the *other* side, not the resource path already identifies). Same
both-sides `update` authorization as `link_related`. `NotFound` when no
live join row matched (already unlinked, or never linked) — same
not-found-not-forbidden convention every other record-scoped mutation in
this module uses.

pre-warm (`registry_ready`, Plan 1.2), and the applied schema version
(P-migration-governance) are all confirmed. Load balancer / Kubernetes
gates traffic on the status code, not the body.

M01 Core C-23: dropped the 422 this operation used to declare — the
handler takes no request body/query/path parameters, so validation
failure was never a reachable outcome here. The genuine non-200 outcome
(503, `not_ready`/`draining`) is this same custom `serde_json::Value`
body, not `ErrorResponse` — see `ready_response`/`draining_response`.

get.summary:
U9-T1 — the startup probe: 200 once this node has finished booting
(migrations, seeds, pre-warm), 503 before. An orchestrator holds liveness
and readiness checks until it passes, so a slow first boot is not killed
as a hung one. Never reads a dependency: readiness does that.

P-deployment-preflight follow-up (deployment manifest) — unauthenticated,
read-only, same convention as `/health`/`/health/ready`/`/health/dependencies`:
an operator or support engineer confirming what a running node actually is,
without needing a shell into the container.
get.description:
`image_digest` is deliberately absent: a running process cannot know its
own image's registry digest (the digest is computed by the registry from
the final pushed layers, after this binary was already built) — that half
of "the deployment manifest" is generated once, at release time, as a
`deployment-manifest.json` release asset instead (see
`document/general/plans/P-deployment-preflight.md`; the GitHub Actions
release workflow that once generated it was retired with the rest of CI).

`configuration_version` (P-environment-promotion §5 step 20, amends the
D-099/D-211-era "same as `application_version`" convention) is the sha256
of this deployment's canonical metadata export
(`xrm_server::bundle::canonical::bundle_hash`) — a real, deployment-
computed fact rather than the binary's own release version, because two
nodes running the identical release can legitimately hold different
metadata (mid-promotion, or a customization). `state.configuration_version`
is set once at the end of `XrmSystem::build()` and again after every
successful bundle apply (`xrm_server::bundle::apply::run_apply_job`); this
is what makes `fleetctl sync`/`drift` (which already compare this field on
every run) the scheduled drift check, with no scheduler inside the
deployment. Falls back to `application_version` — the old value — whenever
nothing has set it yet (attome-server tests, or a boot path that hasn't
reached `XrmSystem::build()`), so every existing call site keeps working.

input_schema.description:
M101 slice 3 — the action's argument contract as a JSON Schema
document, parsed rather than passed through as a string so a consumer
reads structured JSON instead of re-parsing an escaped blob.

Published, not enforced: validation lives in each executor (see
`ActionDescriptor::input_schema`). This is what a tool-listing consumer
— a model picking a tool, an agent-builder UI, an external tool
protocol — needs in order to call an action correctly on the first try.

`value_type = Object` is required, not cosmetic: `serde_json::Value` is
a recursive enum, and letting utoipa derive an inline schema for it
here overflowed even `main.rs`'s 64 MB schema-generation stack
(`server --print-openapi` aborted with 0xC00000FD). Declaring it as a
free-form object stops the recursion and is also the truthful
description — a JSON Schema document is an arbitrary object.

ApprovalPlan.description:
D-421 / M10 (Approval & Governance) — an ordered set of approval steps,
persisted on the request as `plan JSONB` (migration
`0185_approval_request_plan_step.sql`). This is a **pure extension** of
D-195's primitive, not a second one (guidelines §13): a plan-bearing
request is still one `approval_request` row running through
`submit`/`decide`/`sweep_expired`'s same lifecycle machinery — a plan just
tells `decide_step` how many steps there are and what each one requires,
instead of the flat `required_approvals` count every pre-D-421 caller
still uses unchanged.

`mode`/`approvers` (`any`/`all`/`n_of_m` over a list of opaque tokens) is
generic dual-control sequencing — this crate owns it because it never has
to interpret a token to run the math. **What it must never do** is turn a
token like `"role:finance_manager"` or `"position:manager_of_requester"`
into an actual user id — that resolution is XRM metadata knowledge
(roles, teams, org structure) this crate has none of (guidelines §1), so
it stays in `xrm_audit::approval::resolve_step_approvers` (ARCH-5's same
split: attome-approval runs the lifecycle, the engine layer resolves what
its own tokens mean). Every function below that needs "who may decide
this step" therefore takes an already-resolved `&[Uuid]`/`usize` from the
caller — it never touches `approvers` itself.

action's payload (`attome_audit::approval::condition_permits`) — see
that function's doc comment for the fail-closed semantics.

oneOf.description:

allOf.description:

the JSON keys sit on the step itself and a plan stored before them
reads with every default.

approvers.description:

`"role:<uuid>"`. See the module-level doc comment above.

which falls back to manual — see [`Distribution::SkillMatch`]'s doc
comment); must be omitted for `round_robin`/`least_loaded`, whose
target is computed automatically.

reason.description: Q10-T6: why the role was given.

valid_until.description:
Q10-T6: when the grant ends (it is removed then, ending the user's
sessions); absent means it does not end. Must be in the future.

id.description:
`None` when this call only submitted a four-eyes approval request —
mirrors `retention_admin::ActionTransitionResult`'s
`approval_pending`/`approval_request_id` pair.

AttributeDef.description:
`attribute_info` — one field of an entity. `entity_ref` is the
parent [`EntityDef`]; `lookup_entity_ref` is carried as the target's
logicalname. `default_value` is deliberately absent: nothing in the
platform reads or writes that legacy column (the backfill default of a
schema-change plan is not stored on the attribute), and `AttributeDesc`
has no slot for it, so it could never be applied.

is_write_restricted.description:
D-507: writes need a field-security `can_update` grant; reads don't.
`#[serde(default)]` so a bundle authored before D-507 still parses.

purpose.description:
Developer-facing note on why this field exists — locale-less, never
shown to end users (distinct from the label-store `description`,
D-426, which this bundle format does not carry — see `LabelDef`).

AttributeIndexStatus.description:
The current state of the supporting sortable/filterable index. This is
intentionally a separately polled resource: `AttributeMeta` remains a
metadata contract, while queue and Postgres catalog state are transient.

data_classification.description:
P-data-protection-governance §4: `"general" | "personal" |
"sensitive_special_category"` — additive to `is_sensitive` above
(which keeps its narrower audit-masking-only meaning). Always
present, matching the column's `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'general'`.

is_write_restricted.description:
D-507: writing this field's value needs a field-security `can_update`
grant, but reading it does not (unlike `is_sensitive`, which gates
both and masks audit values).

on_target_delete.description:
P-data-lifecycle item (c): `"restrict" | "orphan" | "cascade-deactivate"`
— meaningless for a non-lookup field, always present regardless
(matches the column's `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'orphan'`).

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this field —
`platform | product | project | customer`. Only a changeset of this
layer may change or retire it.

purpose.description:
Developer-facing note on why this field exists / what it's used for —
locale-less, internal, distinct from `metadata_label`'s
per-locale end-user-presentation `description` (D-426). `None` when
never set.

AttributePatch.description:
One field promoted onto an entity this bundle does not otherwise define —
the fix for the gap the verticals skill documents repeatedly (M77/M78/
M82/M74): a vertical needing e.g. `asset_ref` on `service_ticket` (owned by a
different module) previously had no way to add just that field without
including `service_ticket`'s full [`EntityDef`], which would either re-assert
every one of that entity's other attributes or — on a target lacking the
owning module — wrongly create a stub entity from scratch.

The key difference from [`EntityDef`]: [`super::plan::diff_attribute_patches`]
never creates `entity` if it doesn't already exist live. A patch only
ever augments an entity, never brings one into being — see that
function's own doc comment for the exact semantics.

entity.description:
Target entity logicalname. Must already exist on the deployment this
bundle is applied to, or the patch is `Blocked` at plan time.

allowed_cidrs.description:
Client addresses allowed to reach the portal, as CIDRs or single
addresses. Empty means any address. Outside it, every portal route
answers the same 404 as an unknown portal (G-13).

editable_profile_fields.description: `webportal_user` fields a user may edit on their own profile.

page_size_cap.description: The largest page a portal list returns, 1 to 100 (R10, G-13).

records_rpm.description: Portal-wide ceiling on record-route requests per minute (G-4).

row_version.description: Echo it back on the next write (optimistic concurrency).

signup_role_ref.description: The portal role a self-registered or OIDC-created user gets.

trusted_server_login.description:
D-779: the portal's own servers (S2S clients granted
`webportal.trusted_login`) may sign users in with a password and
create accounts for free usernames. Off by default.

username_blocked_words.description: D-777: words no username may contain (case-insensitive).

username_min_len.description: D-777: username length, in characters (defaults 3 and 12).

username_reserved.description:
D-777: whole usernames nobody may take (case-insensitive), e.g.
"admin", "support", staff names.

next_value.description: The next number this counter gives.

sequence_key.description: The rendered sequence key (empty: the rule's single counter).

truncated.description: More than 200,000 values are stored; only that many were read.

duplicates.description: Numbers more than one record holds (at most 100 listed).

missing.description:
Numbers between the rule's initial value and the last one that no
record holds (at most 100 listed).

missing_more.description: More missing numbers exist than are listed.

pattern.description: The stored values of one counter, the number shown as `#`.

unmatched.description: Stored values that do not fit the format (typed by hand or migrated).

entities.description:
Entity logicalnames the Angular shell filters the sidebar tree down
to when this app is selected. A pure UX filter — see this file's own
doc comment; never re-checked as a grant.

AvailableTransition.description:
One entry of `GET /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/transitions` — drives UI buttons
and kanban drop targets. Never lists a transition the caller lacks
`required_privilege` for.

is_mine.description:
`true` for a `personal`/`shared` view the caller themselves owns —
the client-side signal for showing owner-only actions. Never used for
enforcement; the mutating routes re-check ownership server-side.

scope.description:
D-429 — `system` | `personal` | `shared`. Drives whether the Angular
list toolbar offers "edit"/"delete"/"share" for this row (only ever
the caller's own `personal` rows).

files.description: Files listed beside it; `null` when it has no file list.

taken_at.description: When it was taken, from its name.

last_drill.description:
The newest restore drill (U6-T3), as `attome backup drill` and the
monthly run record it.

runs_here.description: Whether this deployment runs the built-in backup (Solo only).

same_disk.description:
True when `backup.dir` is not set, so backups share the database's
machine and disk.

items.description:
At most 100 requests, typically similar ones the administrator
reviewed a sample of (`GET /api/v1/admin/approvals?action_type=...`).

BatchItem.description: One request of a batch, at the version the administrator looked at.

BatchOutcome.description: One request's outcome in a batch.

error.description:
Why this one was not decided (stale version, already decided, the
administrator's own request, ...); `null` on success.

status.description: The request's status after the decision, or `null` when it failed.

BinRestoreFailure.description: One record a restore could not bring back.

code.description:
`not_found`, `forbidden`, `conflict` (live already, or a value now
taken by another record), `invalid` (a lookup it points at is gone)
or `failed`.

oneOf.description:
For `invalid`: a deleted record this one points at, which the caller
may restore first ("Restore parent too", A18-T9).

items.description: At most 500.

BinSetting.description:
One entity's recycle-bin rules (`bin_setting`); an entity with no row
has the defaults.

alert_threshold.description: Deletions by one person within ten minutes that raise an alert.

hard_delete_needs_approval.description: A permanent delete waits for a second person's approval.

require_reason.description: A person must give a reason to delete.

retention_days.description:
Days a deleted record stays in the bin before it is purged; `null`
follows the deployment's `retention.entity_purge_grace_days`.

Block.description:
One block on the canvas. `props` is validated against `kind`'s shape by
`blocks::validate_blocks` before a draft save or publish is accepted —
never stored as trusted-opaque JSON (coding-guidelines §8).

BlockKind.description:
The full block library (mockup's block-library modal). Kept as a real
enum (not a bare string) so an unrecognized `kind` is rejected by
deserialization itself, before `blocks::validate_blocks` ever runs.

items.description:
Every object the apply published, with the version it published and
the one it replaced (pass these to rollback to undo).

BlueprintItem.description: One object of a blueprint and what applying it would do (N12-T3).

id.description: The existing object's id; `null` for a new one.

published_version.description: The version that is published now, which a rollback returns to.

surface.description: The surface filter, or `null` for every surface.

BrandAsset.description: A brand asset of one theme version.

ttl_minutes.description: Window length in minutes. Default 60, maximum 240.

was_open.description: `true` if a window was actually open and is now closed.

approval_pending.description:
D-195 — `true` when `approval.required_actions` names
`metadata.break_glass` (always, on the production profile): nothing
was opened; a second, different `system.admin` must decide the
request via `POST /api/v1/admin/approvals/{id}/decide`.

opened_until.description:
UTC instant the window closes by itself. `None` while the request is
still pending approval.
UTC instant the window closes; `None` when closed.

remaining_seconds.description: Seconds until the window closes; `None` when closed.

field.description:
`"query_id"` or `"view_id"` — which column this broken reference came
from.

reason.description:
`"invalid_format"` (not a UUID at all) or `"not_found"` (well-formed,
but no active row of the referenced kind has that id).

value.description: The raw stored value that failed to resolve.

oneOf.description: The single bucket of an ungrouped definition.
A group whose stored value is not NULL, as PostgreSQL renders it as text.
The group of rows whose field is NULL.

A time bucket: `start ≤ t < end`, both UTC instants computed in the
resolved timezone.
Everything past `presentation.limit`, when `other_bucket` is set.

BucketKey.description:
A bucket's identity: the stored value, never a display string, so a drill
predicate can be rebuilt from it exactly (D-522 decision 11).

BulkCloneFailure.description: One record a bulk clone could not copy.

code.description:
`not_found`, `forbidden`, `invalid` (the copy failed validation),
`conflict` (a unique value) or `failed`.

overrides.description: Values every copy takes in place of its source's, by field.

BulkCloned.description: One record a bulk clone copied.

undo.description: The copy's undo list, as a single clone returns it.

BulkEditPreview.description: B5-T2: what a bulk edit would do, without doing it.

matched.description: Records picked that the caller can read.

samples.description: The first 20 records the edit would change, before and after.

unchanged.description: Picked records already holding the requested values.

BulkEditRequest.description: What to change on the picked records.

filters.description:
The records to change, by the same filters a list uses. At most 500
may match.

ids.description: The records to change, at most 500. Give `ids` or `filters`.

operations.description: The changes, applied in order to each record.

id.description:
The bulk operation applying the edit; follow it at
`/api/v1/{entity}/bulk/{id}`. Empty when no record needed a change.

matched.description: Records picked that the caller can read.

unchanged.description: Picked records already holding the requested values.

undo.description:
B5-T3: what to send to `POST /api/v1/{entity}/bulk-edit/undo` to put
the changed records back. Kept by the caller, like a clone's undo
list.

BulkEditUndoRequest.description: B5-T3: a bulk edit to put back.

undo.description: The `undo` list the bulk edit returned.

BulkFieldMode.description:
`legacy` (0): every non-sensitive field, the behaviour before D-589.
`listed` (1): only the fields in `fields`.

conflict.description:
A16-T6: for a conflict, the record's current version and what changed
since the row's version (`current_version`, `current_state`).

outcome.description:
A16-T6: `ok`, `conflict` (the row's `expected_row_version` was stale;
see `conflict`), `error`, or `pending` while the row has not run.

BulkRecordEnvelope.description:
`pub(crate)` so `bulk_graph.rs`'s pure preflight functions can operate on
the same envelope shape the HTTP layer and the worker already share,
instead of introducing a second, parallel record representation.

skip_defaults.description: A28-T3: create this record without attribute defaults.

apply_defaults.description:
A28-T3: `false` leaves empty fields empty on create instead of filling
them with their attributes' defaults. Default true.

BulkTagFailure.description: One record a bulk tag request could not change.

BulkTagRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/tags/bulk`: add one tag to, or take one tag off,
the selected records.

oneOf.description: The tag to add (an existing one, or a name to find or create).

BulkTagResult.description: What a bulk tag request did.

Bundle.description:
A whole bundle. Component vectors are in a fixed order in the struct and
each is sorted by its logical key once [`Bundle::normalize`] has run —
which [`super::canonical::canonical_json`] always does first.

attribute_patches.description:
Additive cross-module field promotion — see [`AttributePatch`].
Always present; empty when the bundle carries no patches. Never
exported automatically, same posture as [`Bundle::record_sets`]: hand
authored, since export has no way to know which fields on an entity
this bundle doesn't own are "this vertical's".

calendars.description:
D-404 / M83 Phase 1 — business calendars, holidays embedded per
calendar (a holiday has no independent identity outside its
calendar).

format.description: Always [`BUNDLE_FORMAT`] for a bundle this binary wrote.

labels.description:
M05 Phase 1 (D-426) — deployment-scope `metadata_label`
rows. Export-only; see [`COMPONENT_METADATA_LABEL`].

name.description:
M92 Phase 1 — the bundle's own identity: a stable slug an operator
assigns when authoring a named, versioned artifact (a vertical pack,
`bundle-tool export`'s hand-corrected output — see the verticals
skill's "procedure gaps" §2). `None` for an anonymous whole-deployment
export/promotion, which is the common case `export_bundle` produces
and is not itself a "named bundle". Populated identity is what lets
the ledger answer "which bundles are installed, at which versions"
(`bundle_name`/`bundle_version` in `routes::PlanListItem`) and is what
`requires.depends_on_bundles` and `POST …/bundles/{name}/rollback`
key on.

record_sets.description:
Phase 3 (reference data) — see [`RecordSet`]. Always present; empty
when the bundle carries no reference data.

version.description:
Paired with [`Bundle::name`] — `"MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"`, the version this
specific snapshot represents (not a floor; contrast
[`Requires::platform_version`]/[`BundleDependency::min_version`],
which are floors expressed as `">=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"`).

min_version.description:
A floor, `">=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"` (a bare `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` is read
the same way) — the same convention [`Requires::platform_version`]
uses.

BusinessRule.description:
A rule as the admin API returns it: the row, its roles and its policies.
An expression kind carries `expression`/`target_field`/`message`; a business
rule carries `applies_to`/`roles`/`condition`/`policies`.

applies_to_nobody.description: `applies_to = roles` with no live role: the rule applies to nobody.

disabled_reason.description:
Set when a Solution 7 hook turned the rule off (`field_deleted:<f>`,
`field_retyped:<f>`); cleared when an admin turns it back on.

load_error.description:
Why the stored condition or a policy could not be decoded (possible
only by bypassing this API); the registry does not enforce such a rule.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): `platform`, `product`, `project` or `customer`.

warnings.description: Editor warnings (single-rule reads and writes; empty in lists).

BusinessRuleClient.description:
One business rule as the form evaluates it (design §5): `set_value`
policies and advanced-expression conditions stay server-only.

BusinessRuleOp.description:
Leaf operators (string serde). `eq … in` keep `ConditionOperator`'s
meaning; the per-type table is [`ConditionFieldKind::allows`].

BusinessRulePatch.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/admin/business-rules/{id}`: any field of
[`BusinessRuleBody`]; `entity` and `name` may be sent but not changed.

CalendarDef.description:
`calendar` — one named business calendar (D-404 / M83 Phase 1).
Not a generic XRM entity (same posture as `ViewDef`/`view`), so
addressed by `name` alone rather than `(entity, name)`. `working_days` is
a lowercase 3-letter weekday array (`"mon"`..`"sun"`); `hours` is
`{"mon": [{"start_minute": 540, "end_minute": 1020}], ...}`, matching
`calendar.hours`'s jsonb shape exactly (round-tripped verbatim,
not reparsed into a typed shape here — the same posture `ViewDef.
table_definition` already takes for its own opaque jsonb column).

exceptions.description:
D-592 per-date exceptions. `None` (a bundle written before they
existed) leaves the target's exceptions alone; `Some` is the exact
list, keyed by `exception_date`. Export always writes `Some`.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this calendar: `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer
may update or retire it (409 `layer_mismatch` otherwise).

CalendarExceptionDef.description:
One `calendar_exception` row (D-592), embedded under its
calendar and identified by `exception_date` within it.

ranges.description: `[{"start_minute", "end_minute"}]` on that local date; `[]` closes it.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this exception row (it may
differ from its calendar's). Only a changeset of that layer may
remove it.

ranges.description:
Empty: the date is closed. Otherwise these ranges replace the
weekday's hours for that date.

CalendarTimeRange.description: One working range on an exception's date, minutes from local midnight.

CancelTransitionBody.description:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/transition/cancel` — withdraws the record's
open transition approval (requester only) and returns the record to the
state it came from; or, when that approval was already closed without
executing (rejected, expired, invalidated) but the record is still
parked, finishes returning it (the requester or an administrator).

comment.description: Recorded on the audit events. Optional.

CancelTurnView.description: What a Stop request found (C11 B4).

CapabilityPackRef.description:
One pack that contributed to a session's allowed-action set, with the
`row_version` it held at the moment the session started.

The id alone is not enough: packs are versioned, so "which capabilities did
this session hold" must be answerable later without depending on what the
pack says now (D-556 §2). This is the same `{ref, row_version}` pair
`PolicySnapshot::policy_ref`/`policy_row_version` already carries.

CapacityRow.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/resources/capacity` — a single resource's
capacity/demand picture over the requested `[from, to]` period (M72).
See `capacity.rs`'s module doc for the exact arithmetic behind each
field — in short: `capacity_hours` is the platform's default business
calendar over the period, net of approved leave; `allocated_hours` is
`resource_allocation.allocation_percent` prorated by date overlap;
`actual_hours` is `project_time_entry.hours`, unrelated to either.

actual_hours.description:
`SUM(hours)` from `project_time_entry` for this resource, entries
dated within `[from, to]` — what was actually logged, independent of
what was planned.

allocated_hours.description:
`SUM(allocation_percent / 100 * capacity_hours * overlap_days /
period_days)` across every `resource_allocation` row overlapping
the period — prorated against the period's nominal (pre-leave)
capacity, not the leave-adjusted figure above; see `capacity.rs`.

capacity_hours.description:
Business-calendar working hours over `[from, to]`, net of any
`resource_availability` leave overlapping the period.

over_allocated.description:
`allocated_hours > capacity_hours` — the resource is committed past
what the period's business calendar (net of leave) can deliver.

resource_name.description:
`user_account.user_name` — `None` for a legacy row with no
username set, same optionality the column itself carries.

utilization_pct.description:
`allocated_hours / capacity_hours * 100`; `0.0` when `capacity_hours`
is `0` (e.g. a period with no working days at all, or a resource on
leave for the whole period) rather than a division-by-zero `NaN`.

label.description:
A human name for this snapshot (e.g. "Sprint 3 baseline"). Capturing
twice with the same label for the same project is safe — see this
module's doc comment — and returns the existing baseline rather than
creating a duplicate.

item_count.description:
Number of `project_baseline_item` rows captured under this
baseline — every active work item on the project at capture time.

version_no.description: The suite's draft after the case was added.

activity_mapping.description:
Interpretation depends on `source` — see `extraction.rs`'s doc
comment for the exact shape each source kind expects.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this definition.

visibility_privilege.description:
M41 §5 Permissions — a privilege key aggregate DFG/variant views will
require of the caller. Stored and schema-ready; enforcing it on a
self-service (non-admin) read surface is Phase 2+ (Phase 1 exposes
only the admin-gated routes this crate mounts today).

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this definition —
`platform`, `product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of
that layer may change or retire it.

message_id.description: The assistant message that went wrong.

name.description: The case's name; defaults to one naming the message.

to_attribute.description: `None` for an entity-level reference (0356's empty-string sentinel).

ChangeFeedEntry.description:
One row of the unified feed. `reference` is always the id of the actual
source record (not this feed's own bookkeeping), so a caller can follow up
against that source's own admin surface.

actor.description:
Best-effort — `None` when the source records no actor at all (see the
module doc's per-source notes), never fabricated.

ChangeKind.description:
One source this feed aggregates. The wire value (`kind` filter and each
entry's own `kind` field) is this variant's snake_case name.

approval_pending.description:
`true` when this call only submitted a pending four-eyes approval
request rather than deciding the change request immediately —
mirrors `attome-dashboard::lifecycle::PublishResponse`'s own field.

field_type.description: `text | number | currency | date | bool | choice | rich_text`.

ChangesetOperation.description:
One recorded operation as the review sees it (the raw row snapshot stays
server-side; `args` is set once the changeset is closed).

object_ref.description: The live row, for diagnostics; never exported.

apply_ids.description:
Every planned expand row, in apply order — what `apply` takes for
`phase = expand`.

contract_apply_ids.description: Every contract row, in apply order.

ChangesetSummary.description: A changeset without its document or operations.

checksum.description: Set once the changeset is closed (an automatic one: once sealed).

row_version.description: Send as `If-Match` to close or abandon.

citations.description:
C11 B6 (row A-86): on an assistant answer grounded in the widget's
knowledge, the sources it drew on — title and section only. Omitted
when there are none, so a widget that predates it receives exactly the
response it always did. Not stored: a later poll returns the message
without them.

direction.description: `inbound` (the visitor) or `outbound` (the bot, or a human agent).

note.description: Why it is checked out, shown to others (at most 500 characters).

ChildSession.description: One session a supervisor delegated to (N8-T1's run tree).

agent_object_ref.description: The specialist agent object it ran as.

counted.description:
`false` on a table too large to count inline; `values` then lists the
choices with no counts.

ChoiceValueUsage.description: One value of a choice field and the records holding it.

defined.description:
The value is one of the field's current choices; `false` for a value
still stored after it was removed.

CitationView.description:
One citation, projected from `attome_search::KnowledgeCitation` — every field
except `passage`, whose text is already in the turn's tool message. An
explicit shape, never the stored JSON passed through.

data_source_id.description: The Data Source that permissioned it at retrieval time.

fetched_at.description: When a web-sourced passage was fetched; `null` for authored articles.

heading_path.description: The heading path of the cited section, outermost first.

item_id.description: The knowledge article the passage came from.

stale.description: Past its `review_by` date when it was retrieved.

truncated.description: The section was returned in part.

claimed.description:
`false` when the queue is currently empty — not an error, just
nothing to claim right now.

oneOf.description: `None` when no callable member is left.

CloneChild.description:
A child relationship: records of `entity` whose `field` points at the
record being copied.

children.description: Child records to copy with it, by relationship.

overrides.description: Values for the copy that replace the source's, by field.

preview.description: Return the copy's body without creating it.

CloneResult.description: What a clone made, or would make.

body.description: The body sent to the create path.

children.description: The child relationships copied with it.

id.description: The new record's id; absent for a preview.

left_out.description: Fields of the source left out of the copy, and why.

undo.description:
Every record made, children first, at the version it was made with:
the body of `POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/clone/undo`. Empty for a
preview.

CloneUndoItem.description: One record a clone made, at the version the clone left it.

operation_id.description:
Their delete operation:
`POST /api/v1/bin/operations/{operation_id}/restore` brings them back.

removed.description: Records moved to the recycle bin.

ClonedChildren.description: What a clone did with one child relationship.

count.description: Child records found and readable (copied, or that would be).

ids.description: The copies' ids; empty for a preview.

skipped.description: Child records the caller cannot read, left behind.

changeset.description:
The `attome-changeset/v1` document; write it into the repository with
`node scripts/changesets/write-closed.mjs --dir <folder>`.

summary.description:
Plain-language review text (the same wording as
`scripts/changesets/summarize.mjs`).

kind.description:
`non_portable_value` (translation left a deployment-local id out) or
`unrecorded_entity_change` (the metadata change log shows the entity
changed after the changeset opened, and no recorded operation covers
it).

chunks_embedded.description:
Chunks carrying a vector from the configured model. `None` when
knowledge is lexical-only by configuration.

embedding_backlog.description:
Chunks still waiting for a vector from the configured model (never
embedded, or embedded by a different one). `None` when knowledge is
lexical-only by configuration.

items_draft.description: Items waiting in the draft review queue. Never chunked (D-489).

items_total.description: Live items in the collection, whatever their lifecycle.

last_indexed_at.description: The newest `indexed_at` among those chunks; `None` when there are none.

choice_styles.description:
Per-value color/icon presentation hints for a `data_type: "choice"`
column — the raw `choice_styles` map from `attome_field::ChoiceOptions`,
keyed by choice value. `None` for every other column, and for a
choice column with no configured styles. Metadata-derived, set
alongside `data_type` in the enrichment loop below.

lookup_target_entity.description:
Logical name of the entity a `data_type: "lookup"` column points to —
`None` for every other column. Metadata-derived (never from
`table_definition`), set alongside `data_type` in the enrichment loop
below. The frontend turns this into a route
(`logicalToUrlPath`) to make an unconfigured lookup cell clickable by
default — a plain logical name, not a route, so this crate stays free
of Angular's routing scheme.

base_hash.description:
The content hash of the document the commands were made against; empty
for an object that does not exist yet.

name.description: The object's name; required when it does not exist yet.

issues.description: References to objects that do not exist; they do not block the draft.

amount.description: Decimal text; negative takes pay away.

CommissionAdjustmentOutcome.description: The adjustment written, or the approval it waits on.

approval_request_id.description: The approval request, when the amount is above the threshold.

CommissionDisputeDecision.description: A reviewer's decision on a dispute.

amount.description: Required for `adjust`: the adjustment, as decimal text.

CommissionEstimate.description: What one opportunity would pay if it closed now.

payout.description: The opportunity's own payout across the plan's components.

period_change.description:
How the period's total changes with it (more than `payout` when it
lifts every credit into a higher retroactive band).

run_ids.description: One calculation run per plan version.

amount.description: Absent when the caller may not see pay amounts.

explanation.description: A line's explanation steps; an adjustment's reason.

Comparator.description: How one field of a rule compares two records.

CompareMetricColumn.description:
`pub` (this struct and the three below, fields too) — `do_compare`
returns this directly and this crate's own `tests/scenario.rs` inspects
it, same reasoning as `ScenarioResultRow` above.

cells.description:
Aligned by index with the response's `metrics` array — a `null`-shaped
entry (`status = "not_evaluated"`) stands in for a metric this
scenario references but has never run `evaluate` for.

ComparisonReport.description: The whole report: every group matching the filter, plus when it was run.

ComparisonRow.description:
One `(action, model_id, prompt_version)` group's outcome rates, each with
its own Wilson interval sized to that group's own sample.

total_decided.description:
Non-pending outcomes — the denominator every rate below is computed
against. Excludes `pending` for the same reason `quality_monitor.rs`
and `compliance_report.rs` do: an undecided suggestion is neither a
success nor a failure yet.

acceptance_rate.description:
`(accepted + edited) / (accepted + edited + rejected)`. `None` when
there are zero decided outcomes for this model — a rate of "0%" would
misreport "everyone rejected it" when really nobody has decided yet.

approved.description:
`true` when a live `ai_model` catalog row names this model with
`approval_status = 'approved'`.
**`in_use && !approved` is the finding this report exists to catch.**

in_use.description:
`true` when this model has at least one row in
`ai_suggestion_outcome` — it was actually invoked.

outcomes_without_provenance.description:
Governance-sensitive count of `ai_suggestion_outcome` rows missing
model_id/prompt_version/action_id — see this module's doc comment for
why this should always read zero and how it is nonetheless checked as
data rather than assumed from the schema.

channel.description:
`email` or `internal` — Phase 1 accepts no other value (see this
module's doc comment).

recipient_user_ids.description:
Recipient `user_account` ids. Required, non-empty, for
`channel=internal`; ignored otherwise.

to.description:
Recipient email addresses. Required, non-empty, for `channel=email`;
ignored otherwise.

id.description: The record, for update and delete; may be a `${ref.id}` reference.

ref.description:
This operation's name, for later references: lowercase letters,
digits and `_`, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters.

all_or_none.description: Every operation commits or none does. Not available yet (S1-T8).

error.description: The error body, as a single request would have answered.

status.description: The HTTP status the operation would have had on its own.

actual.description:
Required when the metric is `source_kind = "manual"`; ignored for
`"query"`.

force.description:
When `true`, always writes a new snapshot — D-407's restatement path
— chained via `superseded_ref` to whatever was there before, which is
left untouched.

period_start.description:
Defaults to the metric's current period (today's day/week/month/
quarter/year boundary, UTC).

skipped.description:
`true` when an existing snapshot was returned unchanged (idempotent
skip) rather than a new one being computed.

all.description:
The tree nests, so utoipa must not expand it inline (the recursion
would overflow the stack while building the OpenAPI document).

expression.description:
A `attome-rules` expression over the entity's own fields that types as
`bool`. A rule with an advanced leaf may not carry `hidden` or
`disabled` policies (the client cannot mirror it).

value.description: A literal (an array for `in`). Exactly one of `value` and `value_ref`.

value_ref.description:
`@portal_user.id`, or `@portal_user.<lookup field>` (e.g.
`@portal_user.account_ref`). Only with `eq`. Resolved per request; a
null or missing value matches no row.

`field` may be `id`, the record's own key, with `eq` only: that is how
a role reaches the portal user's own parent record
(`id = @portal_user.company_ref`).

ConditionTree.description:
A condition: `{"all": [...]}` (AND), `{"any": [...]}` (OR), a structured
leaf `{"field", "op", "value"?}`, or an advanced leaf `{"expression"}`
holding a `attome-rules` boolean. The root `{"all": []}` means "always".

ConfidenceInterval.description: A Wilson score confidence interval, `[lower, upper] ⊆ [0, 1]`.

ConfiguredAccess.description:
The "configured" half: every raw assignment that feeds resolution, with
display names attached so the UI doesn't need N follow-up lookups.

ConfirmApprovalRequested.description: `202`: a `Consequential` action was submitted for four-eyes approval.

ConfirmConflict.description:
A confirm or reject that did not run anything: the standard error body
(`error` is always `"conflict"` or `"rate_limit_exceeded"`) plus the
outcome decided from the persisted state.

approval_request_id.description: `approval_pending`: the approval request it waits on.

result.description: `already_executed`: the recorded result of the execution that ran.

ConfirmToolCallRequest.description:
Body of `POST …/tool-calls/{tid}/confirm`. **Only the hash the UI
displayed** — the arguments that run are the server's stored copy (I-13).
An `arguments` field, or any other, is rejected (row A-08).

ConflictCount.description: A16-T7: the conflicts of the last `days` days, by entity and source.

accepted.description:
The signed-in user has accepted the current versions (always true when
the portal requires none).

ConsumerHealth.description: L7-T7: how one change-feed consumer is keeping up.

lag_events.description: Events written after its cursor, up to [`LAG_COUNT_CAP`].

lag_seconds.description: Age of its oldest unread event; 0 when it has read everything.

last_event_at.description: The time of the last event it read, if any.

last_read_at.description: When it last advanced its cursor.

status.description: `active`, or `expired` once it fell past its allowed lag.

ContentSpace.description:
A reusable container of pages — a pure organizational grouping, not a URL
namespace (`url_path` uniqueness stays global across all spaces; see
D-369). Infra-mutable class (D-005).

ContrastFailure.description: One pair that reads too faintly, or two status colours too alike.

ratio.description: The measured contrast ratio, or ΔE for `distinct`.

ControlBody.description: A control request: the instance's current `row_version`.

ControlResult.description: The instance's state after a control action.

last_ordinal.description: The ordinal of the last message; the history's `total`.

from_type.description:
The type the caller expects the field to have now; `type_drift` when
it differs. Omitted = the live type.

map.description:
text -> choice: source text -> choice value (the values become the
field's choices).

organization_id.description:
The organization the new project is created under — required because
`organization_id` is a required lookup on `attome_project` and nothing on
`service_work_request` names one.

project_id.description:
The project the new task (`project_work_item`) is created under —
required because `project_id` is a required lookup on that entity and
nothing on `service_work_request` names one.

expires_in_days.description:
P-account-lifecycle — overrides `auth.apikey_default_expiry_days` for
this one key. `None` (the default when the field is omitted) falls
back to the configured default, itself `None` unless an operator set
it — so an old client that never sends this field keeps getting
no-expiry keys exactly as before, unless the deployment opted in.

error.description: Why it would not, as the create would say it.

failures.description: A3-T1: every failing field, when the create failed on its fields.

warnings.description: Business-rule warnings the create would raise.

client_id.description: Machine-readable slug, e.g. "sap-erp". Immutable after creation.

service_user_ref.description:
Required. The `user_account` this client acts as: every
S2S-authenticated request runs with that user's privileges and is
attributed to it in the audit trail. Must reference an existing user.
(`Option` only so a missing value is reported through the JSON
validation contract — `422 validation_error` naming the field — rather
than axum's plain-text body-rejection.)

pages.description:
Same shape `pages_snapshot` produces — every `id` may be omitted, a
fresh one is always generated (`IdPolicy::GenerateNewIds`).

register_link.description:
The fully-qualified register link — handed to an admin to relay to the
invitee directly, since `config.email.enabled = false` (no SMTP
configured) is a fully supported deployment shape (D-002 single-tenant
air-gapped install). Also emailed when `email.enabled` is true, same
dual-path pattern as `register`'s own verification-email step.

CreateInvitationResponse.description:
Only ever returned once, right after minting — same "the caller needs the
actual bearer at least once" reasoning as every other token-issuance
response in this codebase (e.g. MFA's one-time recovery-code batch). Never
re-derivable from `list_invitations`, which only ever returns
`InvitationItem` (no `bearer`/`register_link` field).

scan_schedule.description: A15-T6: `hourly`, `daily` or `weekly` full scans; absent: on demand.

CreateModelBody.description:
`POST /api/v1/admin/predict/models` body. No `features`/`algorithm` field:
Phase 1 has no per-model configurable feature set yet — `features` is
derived and overwritten from `features::FEATURE_KEYS` once training
actually runs (`model::FeatureDescriptor`'s own doc comment), and
`algorithm` is always `logistic_regression` — so accepting either here
