would just be a client-supplied value this crate silently ignores.

template_id.description:
When set, must be one of `content_space_id`'s allowed templates
(`content_space_template`) — its `blocks` are copied into the new
page's `blocks_draft` once, at create time.

entity.description:
Entity logicalname (matches `AvailableViewsQuery.entity` — the shape a
self-service caller already has, unlike the admin `ViewBody`'s
`entity_logical_name: Uuid`, which requires resolving the entity's id
first; that resolution happens server-side here instead).

owner.description: Defaults to the caller when omitted.

format.description:
`csv` or `xlsx` only for this pass — `pdf`/`html` are rejected by the
`format` attribute's `choice` options (see module doc).

parameters.description:
Default parameter filters applied when a run doesn't override them —
same `Filter` grammar `query/execute` and `{entity}/export` already
use, so no new binding/whitelisting surface is introduced.

ip_allowlist.description:
Every entry is validated (`attome_server::middleware::ip_allowlist::
validate_cidr_list`) before the write — a typo'd CIDR is rejected here
at save time rather than silently never matching at request time.

position_hierarchy_enabled.description:
Defaults to `false` — the DB column default (migration 0053); a role
created without specifying this never extends via position hierarchy.

staged_import_id.description:
An `automation_staged_import` id already created via
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/staged-import` (with this project's
`mapping_ref`, and `mode: "dry_run"` for a preview run).

recipients.description:
User emails, team names, or literal email addresses — resolved at
delivery time, not validated against a directory here (same
"opaque until delivery" posture `record_share`'s
principal resolution uses for `user_email`/`team_name`).

expires_in_hours.description: Hours until the link stops working, 1 to 720 (30 days); 72 when absent.

key.description:
For a multi-file field, which stored object to share (one of the
field's keys); ignored for a single-file field.

max_downloads.description: Optional limit on downloads, at least 1.

password.description:
Optional; whoever opens the link must give it. The same strength
rules as an account password apply.

state_field.description: Must name an existing `Choice` attribute on `entity_logicalname`.

filter_event_names.description:
Matches a named change-feed event (`attome_core::change_feed::
emit_named`, e.g. `"sla.breached"`) — migration `0441`,
REVIEW-2026-09-02 finding #3. An unnamed (ordinary) event never
matches a non-null list here.

filter_expression.description:
Reserved for M45 (attome-rules) — stored, never evaluated in Phase 1.
See `attome_events::filter`'s module doc.

config.description:
JSON-encoded adapter config (endpoint templates, pagination style) —
stored as-is; `connector::adapters::rest` reads it once Phase 2 needs
per-system endpoint shaping.

credential_value.description:
Plaintext, accepted exactly once — never stored on the entity row,
never echoed back. Optional: a system can be registered before its
credential is known and rotated in later.

service_principal_ref.description:
The `user_account` id whose `SecurityContext` gates every
write this system's inbound webhook makes (D-425) — see
`system::ensure_service_principal_exists`.

include_patterns.description:
K6-T1 source settings; each one omitted keeps its default (or, on a
re-submitted URL, the value the target already has).

max_depth.description:
Defaults to `config.webcrawl.max_depth` (6) when omitted; clamped to
`MIN_DEPTH..=MAX_DEPTH` regardless of what's requested.

oneOf.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): an approval plan (ordered `any`/`all`/`n_of_m`
steps of `user:`/`role:`/`team:`/`position:manager_of_requester`
tokens), validated with attome-approval's own validator. Requires
`pending_state`.

on_reject_state.description:
An option of the state field; defaults to `from_state`. Only allowed
with `approval_plan`.

pending_state.description:
An option of the model's state field, other than `from_state`,
`to_state` and the model's initial state. Required with, and only
allowed with, `approval_plan`.

request_type.description:
`project_request | change_request | issue_report | it_request |
hr_request | access_request | custom` — the same `service_work_request
.request_type` choice set. Not derived from the offering: an offering
can plausibly back more than one request type, so the caller states
it explicitly, the same "don't guess a product decision" reasoning
`convert.rs`'s required parent lookups already apply.

requester_id.description:
The `user_account` this request is filed on behalf of — the
caller's choice, made explicit, same reasoning as `convert.rs`'s
`project_id`/`organization_id` fields.

portal_token.description:
The self-service portal bearer token (`{public_id}.{secret}`) —
returned exactly once, here. Only its argon2 hash is persisted
(`service_work_request.portal_secret_hash`); this response is the only
place the raw secret ever exists.

CreatedShareLink.description: A new link. `token` and `path` are shown this once.

path.description: The public path to hand out: `/api/v1/shared-files/{token}`.

CursorPage_ChangeFeedEntry.description: The platform's canonical keyset-pagination envelope (guidelines §12), for an access pattern where an exact `total` would need an unbounded scan. `next_cursor` is opaque; `None` means there is no further page. `total`, when present, is the exact size of the whole window; routes that send it send it on the first page only.

items.description:
One row of the unified feed. `reference` is always the id of the actual
source record (not this feed's own bookkeeping), so a caller can follow up
against that source's own admin surface.

actor.description:
Best-effort — `None` when the source records no actor at all (see the
module doc's per-source notes), never fabricated.

total.description:
Exact size of the whole window, when the route counts it (first page
only); absent otherwise.

CursorPage_EvidenceRow.description: The platform's canonical keyset-pagination envelope (guidelines §12), for an access pattern where an exact `total` would need an unbounded scan. `next_cursor` is opaque; `None` means there is no further page. `total`, when present, is the exact size of the whole window; routes that send it send it on the first page only.

outcome.description: The action's outcome, or what a person did with a suggestion.

total.description:
Exact size of the whole window, when the route counts it (first page
only); absent otherwise.

CursorPage_HistoryMatch.description: The platform's canonical keyset-pagination envelope (guidelines §12), for an access pattern where an exact `total` would need an unbounded scan. `next_cursor` is opaque; `None` means there is no further page. `total`, when present, is the exact size of the whole window; routes that send it send it on the first page only.

items.description: One change a history search found.

total.description:
Exact size of the whole window, when the route counts it (first page
only); absent otherwise.

CursorPage_MyWorkItem.description: The platform's canonical keyset-pagination envelope (guidelines §12), for an access pattern where an exact `total` would need an unbounded scan. `next_cursor` is opaque; `None` means there is no further page. `total`, when present, is the exact size of the whole window; routes that send it send it on the first page only.

items.description: One actionable work item, from whichever provider owns it.

actions.description:
Resolved once, at list time, under this same visibility rule —
`actions()` re-resolves them fresh at click time, since eligibility
can change between the two (the plan's "checked at list time and
again at action time").

priority.description:
Free-form, provider-defined (`"high"`/`"1"`/...) — Dashboard does not
interpret it beyond display.

provider.description:
The provider's own `name()` — lets a caller group/filter without a
second lookup. Owned, not `&'static str`: `#[derive(Deserialize)]`
cannot prove a borrowed field outlives an arbitrary deserializer
lifetime, and every construction site already has a `&'static str`
literal to hand, so `.to_string()` there costs nothing that matters.

row_version.description:
The optimistic-concurrency version the item's `actions` routes expect
back, when they take one — for an approval that is the approval
request's current `row_version`, which `POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/
decide` requires. Omitted (`None`) by every provider whose actions
need no version.

source_entity.description:
The owning entity's logical name, for a client that wants to link to
the record or run its own further checks.

state.description: The record's own state/status label, for display only.

total.description:
Exact size of the whole window, when the route counts it (first page
only); absent otherwise.

CursorPage_RecordHistoryChange.description: The platform's canonical keyset-pagination envelope (guidelines §12), for an access pattern where an exact `total` would need an unbounded scan. `next_cursor` is opaque; `None` means there is no further page. `total`, when present, is the exact size of the whole window; routes that send it send it on the first page only.

items.description: One change to a record: who made it, when, and which fields moved.

agent_session_id.description: The agent session that made it, when an agent did.

fields.description: Readable fields only, by field name.

group_id.description:
B2-T1: the change set it belongs to: `batch:<id>` (an import or bulk
action), `agent:<session>`, `run:<correlation id>` (a flow run or other
correlated work), `request:<id>` (one save), else `change:<audit id>`.
Changes with the same value were made together.

total.description:
Exact size of the whole window, when the route counts it (first page
only); absent otherwise.

CursorPage_TimelineEntry.description: The platform's canonical keyset-pagination envelope (guidelines §12), for an access pattern where an exact `total` would need an unbounded scan. `next_cursor` is opaque; `None` means there is no further page. `total`, when present, is the exact size of the whole window; routes that send it send it on the first page only.

items.description: One entry in a record's timeline.

detail.description:
Kind-specific detail (audit operation and readable changed fields,
communication subject/channel, note title, activity type, decision
status, …). A JSON object rather than one struct with mostly-empty
fields across six unrelated shapes.

source_entity.description:
The entity or ledger table the underlying row belongs to —
`audit_header`, `audit_detail` (state transitions),
`communication`, `note`, `activity` or
`dashboard_decision`.

summary.description: Short, human-readable description of the event.

total.description:
Exact size of the whole window, when the route counts it (first page
only); absent otherwise.

DataContract.description: D-525 — the data a widget type is built on.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this domain —
`platform | product | project | customer`.

lookup_match_field.description:
Required (and only meaningful) when `lookup_resolution` is
`"by_natural_key"` — the attribute on the *referenced* lookup entity
to match the source value against.

transform.description:
Nullable M45 expression — see this file's module doc. Never
evaluated anywhere in this worktree.

DdlLogEntry.description: One DDL statement as the ledger recorded it.

statement.description: The DDL text (never values; at most 4000 characters).

statement_kind.description: The statement's leading keywords, e.g. `ALTER TABLE`.

variant.description:
The externally-tagged `EngineJob` variant name (e.g.
`"BulkEntityOperation"`) — never the payload itself.

comment.description:
Optional note explaining the decision, stored on the decision's
`approval_grant` row and in its audit event. Trimmed; blank
is no comment; more than 2000 characters is `422 Validation`.

decision.description: `"approve"` or `"reject"` — any other value is `422 Validation`.

executed.description:
Present only when this decision closed the request as `Approved` and
its action was executed in the same call — see `execute_approved`.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this workflow.

Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this workflow — `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer may
change, publish or retire it.

DefinitionSource.description: Where the executed definition came from.

DeflectionStats.description: Conversations started in the window, as they stand when the report runs.

deflected.description: Not handed off, and the last turn ended `completed`.

engaged.description: With at least one turn outcome. The denominator.

unresolved.description: Neither: not handed off, and the last turn ended otherwise.

DegradedFeature.description: One feature that is down or slow right now.

message_key.description: The translation key of the message to show; never a raw error.

valid_to.description:
Defaults to this request's own `expires_at` when omitted — see
`attome_audit::approval::create_request_delegation`'s doc comment.

DeleteImpact.description:
What deleting the records would do (A18-T4), counted without changing
anything.

blocked_by.description: Records that stop the delete while they point here.

cascades.description: Removed with them (and restored with them).

hidden_dependents.description:
Dependents in entities the caller cannot read exist; they are not
counted here.

orphaned.description: Left pointing at a deleted record.

reason_required.description: The entity's bin setting asks for a reason.

ids.description: The records about to be deleted, at most 500.

deleted_at.description: When it was last changed, which for a deleted record is its deletion.

label.description: The record's primary name, when its entity declares one.

operation_id.description:
The operation it was removed in; restore it whole through
`POST /api/v1/bin/operations/{operation_id}/restore`.

reason.description: Why, when a reason was given.

Density.description: How tightly the product packs its content.

DependentCount.description:
Live records of one entity that point at the records being deleted
through one lookup field.

failed_requests.description: Server errors answered while the node drained; empty when not counted.

kind.description: `start` (process start to ready) or `drain` (shutdown signal to exit).

angular_root.description:
Absolute path of this checkout's `angular/` directory, so the UI can
pre-fill the path box with a directory that will actually pass
`resolve_target_dir` instead of making the user guess it.

suggested_dir.description:
The conventional home for entity overrides — the only subtree from
which `provide-xrm-forms.ts` can import with a library-safe relative
path, and therefore the only one this tool auto-registers.

DiffLine.description: One line of a line-based diff between two prompt versions.

DiscoveredModel.description:
One model as the provider reports it. Only the two fields an operator needs
to choose from, deliberately: everything else in a provider's listing
(pricing, ownership, capability flags) varies per protocol and is authored
on the `ai_model` catalog row by the admin, not imported.

The transport half — the request, the capped body read, the parsing and the
masking — lives in `attome_inference::list_models` (BIN-D3), because a
provider record and `config.inference.generation` describe the same kind of
destination and must not disagree about how it is reached. This type stays
here because it is the API's wire shape (`ToSchema`), which the transport
crate has no business knowing about.

display_name.description:
A human label when the provider offers one — Anthropic spells it
`display_name`, and several OpenAI-compatible gateways spell it `name`
(verified live against one that lists 71 models that way). `None` for a
listing that carries only ids, which is what OpenAI's own `/models`
returns.

id.description:
The wire id to send as `model` — what `ai_model.provider_model_id`
holds, and what the D-491 approval gate matches on.

created_at.description:
Some pre-provisioned `attome_document` tables predate the standard
`created_at` system column. Keep the tree endpoint usable for those
tables; the UI renders an unavailable date as `--`.

file.description:
`NULL` for a row whose two-phase create (empty row -> upload session
-> PATCH the key on, see the Angular component's doc comment) never
reached the PATCH — an abandoned or failed upload. Decoding this as a
plain `String` used to panic on exactly that row and abort the whole
connection (D-36x follow-up), taking every other document in the
folder down with it. The UI renders a `null` file as a failed row the
caller can still select and delete.

dsr_requests.description:
Best-effort: only a fulfilled/blocked request carries any entity
association at all (via its `evidence_ref`'s scope list, written at
fulfillment time) — `dsr_admin::create_request` is deliberately
entity-agnostic (a bare subject reference), so a still-pending
request cannot yet be attributed to a domain. See this file's header
note.

last_review_date.description:
Best-effort proxy: this domain row's own `updated_at` (the last time
its steward/deputy/membership assignment was edited through this
admin surface), not a genuine review-cadence tracker — this platform
has no M03 access-review workflow yet to record an actual review
event against.

open_issues.description:
Always empty today — M13 (duplicate queues) and M14 (quality issues),
the plan's named sources of "open issues", are not built yet. Kept as
its own field (rather than omitted) so a future session wires a real
source in without a breaking response-shape change.

pages_needing_root_section.description:
Pages with no active section — reported, never repaired on read
(D-527); `POST .../pages/{page_id}/root-section` repairs one.

sections.description: Every active section under those pages, ordered by `sequence`, then id.

widgets.description: Every active widget under those sections, ordered by `sequence`, then id.

DriftDiff.description: Live metadata planned against the last applied bundle.

clean.description: Every line is `noop` — nothing differs from the applied bundle.

live_hash.description: Hash of the live export at the time of the call.

oneOf.description:
`None` when nothing has ever been applied — then there is no drift
to speak of, and `drift` is `None` too.

DsrScope.description:
`pub(crate)`/`Serialize` (beyond the `Deserialize` every other body-only
struct in this file needs): `approval_admin::gate`'s payload round-trips
through `approval_request.payload` (JSONB) as an opaque `Value`,
and `execute_approved`'s `ACTION_DSR_FULFILL_ERASURE` arm deserializes it
straight back into `Vec<DsrScope>` — reusing this type there rather than
duplicating its two fields, same as every other wired action_type's
payload struct lives next to its own flow, not in `approval_admin.rs`.

match_attribute.description:
Attribute logicalname identifying the subject within this entity
(e.g. `"email"`) — validated against the entity's live registered
attributes before use.

target_section_id.description:
Defaults to the source widget's own `section_id` when omitted —
"duplicate in place" and "paste into another section" are the same
call with/without this field.

record_id.description: The record being edited, never its own duplicate.

values.description: The record's values, as a create or update would send them.

action.description:
What saving would do: `warn`, `allow_with_reason` or `block`; `null`
when nothing matches.

hidden.description: Matches the caller may not read.

DuplicateMatch.description: One existing record a save matches.

score.description: The rule's score for the pair, 0 to 1.

op.description:
`set` (to `value`), `clear`, `add` or `remove` (values of a
multi-select choice), `increment` (a number by `value`, may be
negative).

EffectiveAccess.description:
The "effective" half: `SecurityContext` fields as actually resolved right
now, uncached. `privileges` is sorted (the resolver's `HashSet` has no
stable order) so the UI renders a deterministic list, not one that
reshuffles on every refresh.

record_id.description: Populated by whatever record page embeds this dashboard (Phase 14).

portal_user_field.description:
A lookup on the entity to `webportal_user`, set to the portal user
on every portal create. `null` to clear.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this default share.

business_key.description:
Solution 7 Phase 2 (D-787 rule 7): the declared business key; `null`:
none.

business_key_index.description:
The unique index that enforces the key (`uxbk_<e40>_<h8>`); `null`
without a key.

business_key_index_state.description:
`none` (no key), `missing`, `building`, `invalid` (a failed build;
the next sync rebuilds it) or `valid`.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this entity.

EntityMappingInfo.description:
Response shape for [`QueryDetail::entity_mappings`] — echoes the input
shape plus the resolved `entity_ref` for a caller that wants to cross-
reference `entity_info` without a second lookup.

business_key.description:
Solution 7 Phase 2 (D-787 rule 7): the declared business key — the
1–4 fields its records are matched by, in order; `null`: none.

business_key_index_sync.description:
PATCH only, when the business key changed: how its unique index was
brought in line — `inline`, `queued` (a background job; read its state
on GET), or `failed` (the key is declared but not yet enforced; see
the server log, and GET's `business_key_index_state`).

category.description: Admin-assigned grouping label (e.g. "Account Management"); `None` when uncategorized.

is_reference_data.description:
A configuration-like entity whose records move between deployments
in changesets (`upsert_record`); always has a business key.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this entity —
`platform | product | project | customer`. Only a changeset of this
layer may change or retire it.

EntityRecordResponse.description: One record of any entity. P-api-contract Phase 1: the platform dispatches generic CRUD from runtime metadata (D-003), so `data`'s property names differ per entity and per deployment and cannot be enumerated in a static document — call `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields. Everything outside `data` is the same on every entity.

approval_request_id.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): present only on the response to an update that
asked for a state transition requiring approval. The record was moved
to the transition's pending state (visible in `data`) instead of the
requested one, and this is the approval request that decides it
(`/api/v1/approvals/{id}/decide`). Omitted on every other response, so
those stay byte-identical.

created_at.description:
UTC ISO-8601. Typed `Value` in Rust because it is read straight out of
the dynamic row, but it is always a timestamp string or `null`.

data.description:
The record's own columns, keyed by attribute logical name. Values are
whatever the attribute's field type maps to in JSON.

duplicate_warnings.description:
A15-T4: the existing records this create or update matches under a
`warn` (or reasoned `allow_with_reason`) duplicate rule — the write
succeeded. Omitted when there are none.

expanded.description:
S1-T4: with `?expand=`, the records the named lookups point at, keyed
by lookup attribute; a target the caller may not read is absent.

hidden_duplicates.description: A15-T4: how many more matches the caller may not read. Omitted when 0.

lookups.description:
P-entity-contract-hardening item (a) â€” supersedes D-057's read-time
nulling (DECISIONS.md). `data` always carries the stored UUID for a
lookup field, unmodified; this sibling map carries the tombstone
metadata a client needs instead of a fabricated `null`. `None` (and
therefore omitted from the JSON body â€” `skip_serializing_if`) for any
entity with no populated lookup fields, so a non-lookup entity's
response is byte-identical to before this field existed.

merged_into.description:
A15-T5: this record was merged into that one (the entity keeps merged
records); omitted otherwise.

warnings.description:
D-791 rule 6: the `warning`-severity business-rule `error` policies
that fired on this create, update or upsert — the write succeeded;
the form shows them. Omitted when there are none (and on reads), so
every other response stays byte-identical.

business_rules.description:
D-789 §5 (additive): the active business rules that apply to the
caller and carry a client-side policy (`hidden`, `disabled`, or an
`error` attached to a field) under a structured condition. The form
mirrors them for UX only; the server enforces every write.

EnvVariable.description: One variable: its definition and this deployment's value.

is_set.description: Whether this deployment set a value.

value.description: This deployment's value; always absent for a secret.

EnvVariableChange.description: One change to a variable's value.

value.description: The value set; absent for a secret.

ErasureRequest.description: One erasure request, as staff see it.

ErrorCode.description:
Every `error` code the API answers with.

`not_found`: No such resource, or the caller may not see it.
`unauthorized`: Missing or invalid credentials.
`forbidden`: The caller lacks the privilege for this action.
`attribute_not_writable`: The write sets an attribute the caller may not write; `field` names it.
`limit_exceeded`: The request is past a limit; `limit`, `value` and `next` say which and what to do.
`conflict`: The request conflicts with the current state.
`version_conflict`: The record changed since the caller read it; read it again and retry.
`duplicate_detected`: The save matches existing records under a blocking duplicate rule.
`idempotency_conflict`: The idempotency key was used for a different request.
`validation_error`: The request failed validation.
`rule_violation`: A business rule refused the write; `rule_id` names it.
`field_locked`: A business rule locks a field the write changed.
`field_locked_required`: A locked field is required and was left empty.
`feature_unavailable`: The feature is not available on this deployment.
`feature_hidden`: The feature is switched off for this deployment.
`rate_limit_exceeded` (retryable): Too many requests; wait for `Retry-After`.
`overloaded` (retryable): The server is overloaded; retry shortly.
`capability_unavailable` (retryable): A service the request needs is down; retry after `Retry-After`.
`metadata_authoring_locked`: Metadata changes are locked on this deployment.
`transition_not_allowed`: The state model does not allow this change of state.
`reauth_required`: The action needs a fresh sign-in or second factor first.
`server_timeout` (retryable): The request took too long; it may be retried.
`query_timeout`: An interactive query ran past its limit; run it as an export.
`read_only` (retryable): Changes are paused on this deployment; reads still work.
`payload_too_large`: The request body is too large or too deeply nested.
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`: An earlier attempt with this key did not finish; its outcome is unknown.
`idempotency_replay_unavailable`: The stored response for this key can no longer be replayed.
`method_not_allowed`: The path exists but not for this method; see `Allow`.
`internal_error` (retryable): An unexpected error; the request id finds it in the logs.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

outcome.description: The action's outcome, or what a person did with a suggestion.

next_cursor.description:
Present only in cursor mode: the `after_id` value the caller passes
back to fetch the next page. `None` means either OFFSET mode, or
cursor mode with no further rows (the page came back short).

total.description:
`None` in keyset/cursor mode (P1.11(g)) — `COUNT(*) OVER()` scans the
full matching set regardless of OFFSET vs keyset, a cost independent
of (and additional to) the O(offset) problem keyset fixes, so cursor
requests skip it rather than pay for a total the typical cursor
caller (export/infinite-scroll/API integration) doesn't need.

total_estimated.description:
A13-T2: `true` when `total` is the planner's estimate rather than a
count: a matching set of [`EXACT_TOTAL_LIMIT`] rows or more is not
counted, as counting it would scan it all.

can_edit_query.description:
The caller may open the admin query editor for this exact query.
Query mutations are currently system.admin-only, so derive this from
the same authoritative SecurityContext that authorized execution.

entity_logical_name.description:
Logical name resolved from the query's entity UUID link. Clients use
this to derive generic list/form routes without hardcoded entity URLs.

view_id.description: Presentation view used for this execution. Raw query executions have no view.

view_kind.description:
D-429's view `kind` (chart follow-up, migration 0447) — `None` when
this execution has no bound view. Lets a non-admin client (e.g. the
dashboard widget viewer) render `kind`-specific settings without a
second, admin-gated call — see `SqlQueryRow::view_kind`'s doc comment.

after_id.description:
P1.11(g)/P-stored-query-containment phase 2: the id of the last row
the caller already has. `Some` continues an existing keyset/cursor
page; `None` with `include_total: false` (the default) still runs in
cursor mode, starting from the beginning of the set — see
`config.query.cursor_default`. `page`/`page_size` (offset math) are
ignored whenever cursor mode is in effect.

entity.description: Fallback: entity name string — backend derives UUID via entity_info

entity_logical_name.description: Entity UUID (from entity_info) — backend looks up default view

include_total.description:
P-stored-query-containment phase 2 / D-126: `true` is the only way to
get an exact `COUNT(*) OVER()` total — the full-set window scan is
expensive enough (audit finding #25) that it is opt-in, not the
default, now that cursor mode (below) is the default execution mode.
Defaulting this to `false` (was `true` pre-phase-2) is the one
behavioral flip this plan makes to the wire contract.

order_dir.description:
`"asc"` or `"desc"` — see `Filter::op`'s doc comment for why this
isn't expressed as a JSON-schema `enum` constraint (P-api-contract
Phase 0 disclosure: same reason applies here).

page.description:
One-based — the first page is `page=1` (D-347). Unlike the platform's
`GET` list endpoints, which clamp an out-of-range page, this one rejects
`page < 1` with 422; `page > 10000` is likewise rejected rather than
clamped, to push large scans onto `after_id` (D-031).

query_version_id.description:
D-521 — pinned execution: run this exact immutable
`sql_query_version` instead of the query's current SQL. The
version must belong to the resolved query and the query must still be
active. Only the SQL text, relation inventory and cost estimate come
from the pinned version; `required_privilege`, record-level scope and
the cost ceiling are evaluated at run time exactly as for an unpinned
call (pinned SQL, live security). A published dashboard records the
version each widget was published with and executes it through this.

oneOf.description:
M01 Core P3 gap (D-455) — narrows a single-entity query to rows
linked, through a named M:M relationship, to one anchor record on
the relationship's other side. `AppError::Validation` (422) for a
multi-entity/custom-SQL query (`entity_logical_name.is_some()` is
false — there is no single attribute set / entity for a relationship
to resolve against, the same D-057 boundary record-level RLS
scoping already draws in this file) or for a relationship that
exists but does not connect this query's entity.

seek.description:
AA4-T4: start a keyset page at this sort value ("jump to M", "jump
to March"): the first page holds the rows whose `order_by` value is
at or after it (at or before it for `desc`), with a `next_cursor` as
usual. Coerced and bound like a filter value on the sort column, so a
value of the wrong type is a 422; no rows are counted to find the
place. Not with `after_id` (422).

select.description:
S1-T1: the attributes to return, in this order; `id` is always
included. Absent returns the query's full column list. A name the
query does not return, or one the caller may not read, is the same
422 `unknown attribute`.

view_id.description: Direct list/view selection. The view resolves to its referenced SQL query.

value_display.description:
A readable value where one is safe to show: a built-in `@current_user`
shows only the caller's own user name.

ExplainedPassage.description: One retrieved passage and the terms that brought it.

matched_terms.description: Terms found in the title, headings or passage.

matching_rows.description:
How many rows matched the filter when the export was accepted (the
worker re-resolves the caller's scope when it runs, so the file can be
smaller if access was revoked in between).

columns.description:
Requested column projection. Empty means "every column the caller
can currently read" — resolved fresh by the worker, not frozen at
request time.

FavouriteItem.description: One kept item, as the caller may see it now.

deleted.description: A record deleted since it was kept.

FavouriteItemInput.description: One item to keep in a list.

entity.description: The record's entity; required for a record.

label.description: What to show; a record's own name wins when it has one.

ref.description: The record id, the view id, or the page's route.

FavouriteList.description: One list: the caller's own (`team_id` null) or a team's.

FavouriteListInput.description: A list's whole content, as saved.

items.description: In display order.

FeatureFlagPolicy.description:
The stored policy value for one flag (`setting.value` under the
`feature.*` namespace). All three targeting tiers the M95 plan calls for,
plus the optional progressive-rollout percentage, live in one blob — see
the module doc for why.

percentage.description:
`0..=100`. When present, `deployment: true` is additionally narrowed
to a deterministic hash-of-user-id bucket of that size — the same
user always lands on the same side of the line while the percentage
stays fixed, and a wider rollout only ever adds users, never drops
one already in.

role_overrides.description:
Privilege key -> override. A caller holding any matching privilege is
in scope; "most permissive role wins" if more than one matches (same
posture the record-level access-level resolution uses elsewhere in
this codebase). Checked after `user_overrides`, before the
deployment/percentage tier.

user_overrides.description: Stringified user UUID -> explicit override. Highest precedence.

FeedbackStats.description: Votes on turn answers written in the window.

answers.description: Rateable messages: an assistant message with a terminal state.

rated_answers.description: Answers with at least one vote.

FeedbackView.description: The caller's current vote on one answer.

api_protocol.description:
The protocol the listing was performed under, echoed so a UI can label
results that arrived before an operator changed the field.

FieldChangeResult.description: What a structure change did, or (dry run / blocked) would do.

applied.description: The change committed (or, for a large table, was queued: see `run_id`).

archived.description: Values archived by this call (0 while a large run is still going).

error.description:
A stable refusal code when the change is blocked
(`rename_blocked_by_reference`, `field_referenced`, `field_in_use`,
`archive_key_missing`, ...); `blockers` lists why.

labels.description:
Labels applied by these changes: "runs without business rules or
workflows" on a conversion.

not_convertible.description: Values that do not convert (dry run: would become empty).

nulled.description: Values nulled by a conversion (0 while a large run is still going).

records_with_value.description: Records that keep a removed choice value (shown empty).

report.description:
Release-report items (also stored in the report): breaking API changes,
adjusted/removed customer objects, archived/nulled values.

run_id.description:
The batched run of a large table (`GET .../data-steps/{run_id}` lane
P2-C/E; the run row is `data_step_run`).

sample_record_ids.description: Up to ten record ids of non-convertible values (ids only).

values_to_archive.description: Non-null values the delete archives (dry run: would archive).

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

key_a.description:
Each record's key for a key comparator (phone, email, id, name,
phonetic); `null` otherwise or when the record has none.

score.description: 1 matched, 0 differed, `null` no evidence (a side without a value).

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this member row.
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this profile.

allow_sensitive.description: Required to list an `is_sensitive` field at all.

oneOf.description:
The viewer is authorized to see this value, but this API does not
decrypt it yet — see this module's doc comment.

Hidden: the viewer cannot currently read this field (I7), the whole
record's access has been revoked, or the value is `Restricted`-mode
and `audit.view_sensitive` does not exist yet (Phase 6.6).
Erased via a DSR/retention erasure pass.

FileCheckoutStatus.description: `GET …/checkout`: the lock, when one is held.

uploaded_by.description: The staff uploader; `None` for a portal user's upload (D-774).

uploaded_by_portal_user.description: The portal uploader, for a portal user's upload (D-774).

Filter.description:
P-api-contract Phase 0 disclosure: the retired hand-written
`openapi/query-v1.json` declared `op` as a JSON-schema `enum` of the 8
operator strings in this doc comment. Reproducing an exact `enum`
constraint on a plain `String` field (as opposed to a real Rust enum)
needs utoipa's `schema_with` escape hatch, whose exact builder-call shape
this session could not verify against the installed utoipa version — no
Rust toolchain in this sandbox (see the `no-rust-toolchain` memory /
DECISIONS.md entry for this change). Left as a documented, lower-fidelity
field (doc comment + example) rather than guessing at unverified macro
internals; re-add the `enum` constraint via `schema_with` once a human
can compile-check it — tracked as a Phase 0 follow-up, not silently
dropped. Runtime validation is unaffected either way: every caller's own
`match f.op.as_str()` is untouched by this OpenAPI-only annotation.

op.description:
One of: `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `contains_any`,
`contains_all`, `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`,
`is_null`, `is_not_null`. `starts_with`/`ends_with` are text-only,
like `contains`; `neq` excludes a stored NULL (SQL `<>`), exactly like
every other comparison — `is_null` is the only way to match one. The
four were added by D-607 (advanced find, B-R10 Phase A): the entity
grid had offered them since C-28 while the server refused them. For a
multi-select Choice:
`contains` tests one option, `contains_any` matches any supplied
option, and `contains_all` matches every supplied option. `in` matches
any of a non-empty string array by typed equality (not valid for a
multi-select Choice). `is_null` takes no value and matches a stored
NULL — the only way to express a NULL bucket (dashboard 10/10 Phase 0
spike S1). `under` and `above` (A17-T2) take a record id for a lookup
into a tree (an entity with one parent lookup to itself) and match
that record and everything below it, or above it, up to 32 levels.
`tagged` (B4-T4) takes a tag id on the `id` field and matches the
records carrying that tag (a personal tag only for its owner).

value.description:
Scalar filters retain the v1 string contract. Multi-select Choice
filters additionally accept a JSON string array for `contains_any`
and `contains_all`; `in` takes a string array; `is_null` ignores it.

FilterOrigin.description:
Where an applied filter came from — carried to the response so the
explanation (Phase 3.2) and the records drill use the same list.

attribute.description: The attribute, when the finding is about one.

created_at.description:
A folder is a virtual grouping, not a single row, so this is the
earliest timestamp among everything that makes the folder exist: the
explicit `document_folder.created_at` if it was created
empty, and/or the earliest `created_at` of any document living under
it. `NULL` only when the folder path predates the standard
`created_at` column on some pre-provisioned tables.

folder.description:
Full path from the record's root, e.g. `uploads/Contracts` — pass
straight back as the next request's `folder` param to drill in.

entity.description: The entity's logical name, as the record API addresses it.

ai.description: An AI attribute (N11-T1): `record.ai_field` can suggest its value.

attribute.description: The attribute's logical name: the key of its value in a record.

admin_override.description:
P-data-protection-governance §4 cross-border transfer gate. Set only
once an admin has separately confirmed the export destination is
authorized to receive out-of-region restricted data — every use is
logged (`tracing::warn!`), never silent.

id.description: The DSR request this export fulfilled.

GapTopic.description:
A row of the authors' knowledge-gap queue (D-452; surfaced by D-489).

The phrase is the scrubbed topic, never the caller's raw question — read
[`normalize_gap_phrase`]'s doc before widening anything here, and D-452
before changing what a row stores.

addressed_item_ref.description:
The Knowledge Base item that addressed this gap (D-489, migration
0300). No FK: the target is a runtime-provisioned entity table.

addressed_page_ref.description: The content page that addressed this gap, from the 0263 shape.

GoogleConfigInfo.description:
P-frontend-baseline step 5 (D-071/D-073) — closes the config-debt item:
the Google OAuth client id (`config.auth.oauth_google_client_id`, already
the value `google_login` verifies the ID token's audience against) is
served from here instead of being duplicated as a hardcoded literal in
Angular's `environment.ts`. Same "public directory, never a secret" shape
as `OidcProviderInfo` — a client id is not sensitive (it's visible in any
browser's network tab once the Sign-In button loads), only
`oauth_google_client_secret` must never leave this struct.

client_id.description:
`None` when Google sign-in isn't configured for this deployment — the
login page renders no Google button, same as an empty OIDC directory.

GovernanceView.description:
The governance in effect for a conversation's session — snapshotted when
it started (D-505), shown whatever state the session is now in.

state.description:
`"live"` | `"paused"` | `"ended"` — ended covers revoked, ended and
expired alike.

tainted.description: Whether the session started downstream of tool-obtained content (I-10).

GrantView.description:
A grant as stored, with the G-3 label: `public` when no condition is bound
to the portal user, which only a read-only grant may be.

edge_type.description:
`"lookup:{field}"`, `"hierarchy:{field}"`, or `"relationship:{type}"`
— typed by source, per the plan's response contract.

Grounding.description:
Whether a turn's answer is grounded in retrieved knowledge. Decided from
the turn's executed knowledge actions alone — never from the answer text.

oneOf.description: Present only for a time bucket; the field must then be a date field.

HandoffStats.description: Completed agent `bot.handoff` invocations in the window.

blocking.description:
Phase 3.5 — what refuses publish; empty from `do_health_check` alone,
filled by the health route.

checked.description:
Non-empty `query_id`/`view_id` references checked across this
dashboard's widgets — a widget declaring both counts as two; a widget
declaring neither (rich text, dividers, …) is not counted at all.

live_snapshot_format.description: D-543 — the live snapshot's format. `None` when nothing is live.

live_version_dependencies.description:
D-521 — the query versions the **live** version is pinned to, and
whether each has been superseded. Empty when nothing is live or the
live snapshot predates pinning (snapshot format 1).

partially_pinned.description:
True when something is live but its snapshot predates format 3, so some
of what viewers see is still resolved live (view semantics, column
metadata, parameters, variables), or predates format 4 while it has
governed KPI widgets (D-544). Cleared by republishing.

publishable.description: Whether publish would pass the gate now.

warnings.description: Phase 3.5 — what is reported but never blocks.

gregorian_start.description: The Gregorian day the month starts on, as announced.

reason.description: Who announced it, or why; kept on the audit event.

HijriDateBody.description: A Hijri date on the wire (AG1-T6).

gregorian_end.description: The day after the month's last day.

HistoryCompare.description: How a value is compared in a history search.

HistoryMatch.description: One change a history search found.

HistoryRestoreRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/history/restore`: name one change
(`audit_id`) or one change set (`group_id`); `fields` narrows it.

fields.description: Only these fields (logical names); all the change touched when absent.

group_id.description:
A `group_id` from the history: every change of that set to this record
is undone, each field going back to its value before the set began.

oneOf.description: AG1-T6: the day as a Hijri date, stored as its Gregorian day.

holiday_date.description: The Gregorian day. Give this or `hijri_date`.

HolidayDef.description:
One `calendar_holiday` row, embedded under its calendar.
Identified by `holiday_date` within its calendar (D-592); `name` is a
label, so "Eid al-Fitr" can appear once per year.

holiday_date.description:
`YYYY-MM-DD` — a specific date, not a recurring rule (M83 §5:
"Holidays... stored per calendar", no recurrence in Phase 1).

oneOf.description: AG1-T6: the same day in the deployment's Umm al-Qura calendar.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this holiday row (it may
differ from its calendar's: a project may add a holiday to a platform
calendar). Only a changeset of that layer may remove it.

IdentityLinkInfo.description:
P-federation-linking-policy §4.3(a) UI support — `GET
/api/v1/auth/identity-links`'s response shape; see `identity_links`. One
entry per `user_identity` row linked to the caller, plus (since this
entry extends §4.3(a) to Google) at most one synthetic `provider_key:
"google"` entry when `user_account.google_sub` is set. Never includes
`provider_sub` — the IdP-issued subject identifier is an internal
correlation key, not something the UI needs to render a "linked" badge.
`linked_at` is `None` only for that synthetic Google entry — Google has no
per-link timestamp column (see `list_identities_for_user`'s doc comment).

allow_retire.description: Without it every would-be retire is reported as `blocked` (§4).

drafts.description: The drafts saved, in file order.

IndexerStatus.description: The indexer's own state, shared by every collection.

drain_last_advanced_at.description:
When the search drain last advanced its cursor over the change feed —
the last time it processed any entity write, knowledge or not (or,
before its first event, when it first started). `None` when no drain
has ever started.

embedding_model.description:
The model chunk vectors are written with, or `None` when knowledge is
lexical-only by configuration.

duplicates.description: Records whose idempotency key was already stored.

version.description: The highest changeset of the pack applied.

expires_at.description: When the emailed link stops working. The link itself is never returned.

args.description:
The action's own arguments. Shape is per-action and validated by the
executor, not here — a handler that understood every action's argument
shape would be the business logic guidelines §12 keeps out of transport.

remaining.description: Linked values still unrestored (repeat the request when above 0).

id.description: Absent for a notification, which takes no response.

secret.description: Raw HMAC secret — shown exactly once. Store it securely; it cannot be retrieved again.

json_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the kind's documents.

KnowledgeCitation.description:
One passage returned from the knowledge corpus, with everything a citation
needs to resolve (`P-knowledge-base` §8, §11).

Every field is captured at projection time or computed here, never
reconstructed from the article at render time: an item edited after the
answer was generated would otherwise produce a citation pointing at a
heading that no longer exists.

data_source_id.description:
The Data Source that permissioned it — the collection `readable_collections`
resolved for this caller before the query ran.

fetched_at.description: When a web-sourced chunk was fetched. `None` for authored articles.

heading_path.description:
The heading path captured when the chunk was written, outermost first.
Empty for an article's lede, which precedes any heading.

item_id.description: The article record the passage came from.

passage.description: The enclosing section, not the matched chunk. See `expand`'s doc.

stale.description:
Past its `review_by` date. Computed server-side from a plain DATE
comparison, and it reaches a prompt only as untrusted context.

truncated.description:
The section exceeded the passage ceiling and was returned in part.
Reported so an answer can say so rather than presenting a fragment as
the whole.

KnowledgeExplanation.description:
Why a retrieval returned what it did, for an administrator (roadmap
N15-T4): the terms the question was reduced to, the words dropped as
function words, and for each passage, in rank order, which terms it
matched. Retrieved under the administrator's own permissions, lexical
mode, and never recorded as demand or as a gap: explaining a question is
not asking it.

empty_reason.description:
Set when nothing was found: `no_terms` (only function words),
`no_readable_collection` or `no_match`.

terms.description: The content terms, normalised and stemmed as the index stores them.

service_scoped.description:
Always true: governed KPIs are computed by the platform service account
for a fixed scope, never filtered to the viewer (D-522 decision 5).

Always true: computed by the platform service account for a fixed scope,
never filtered to the viewer, and never drillable to records.

oneOf.description: The latest point; `null` unless `status` is `ok`.

history.description: Newest first; a trendline's series, empty for a scorecard.

pinned_query_version_id.description: The query version a published query-backed metric is held to.

attribute_logicalname.description:
Required for `attribute`/`choice_option`; ignored for `entity` (the
entity's own logicalname is always used).

object_kind.description:
`entity`, `attribute`, or `choice_option` — the only kinds this route
accepts (see the module doc).

LabelDef.description:
M05 Phase 1 (D-426) — one `metadata_label` row: a per-locale
override of `object_ref`'s display name/description. `object_ref` is the
same logical-key shape the table itself uses (never a UUID — see
`0201_xrm_core_metadata_label.sql`'s header for the per-`object_kind`
shape), so a label survives round-tripping between deployments the same
way every other bundle component does.

object_ref.description:
Full stored key — `"{entity_logicalname}"` for `entity`,
`"{entity_logicalname}.{attribute_logicalname}"` for `attribute`,
`"{entity_logicalname}.{attribute_logicalname}.{option_value}"` for
`choice_option`.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this label —
`platform | product | project | customer`.

enabled.description: Metrics are on in this process (`observability.metrics_port` set).

routes.description: Every route seen since this process started, slowest p95 first.

LedgerHead.description: The newest ledger row of one (layer, scope).

last_applied_seq.description:
The highest `seq` of this (layer, scope) whose effects are in place
(`succeeded` or `adopted`); `null` when none is.

LedgerRow.description: One ledger row with its document and plan.

cursor.description: Index of the next operation to apply; a resumed run starts here.

LedgerSummary.description: One ledger row without its document and plan.

id.description: The other side's record id to link/unlink.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

code.description: The current TOTP code, when the account has MFA enrolled.

email.description:
The email; kept for clients from before `login` (D-777). Ignored when
`login` is set.

login.description: D-777: the username or the email (an email contains `@`).

LookupMeta.description:
The per-lookup-field value inside `EntityRecordResponse::lookups`. Declared
only so the generated contract (and any client generated from it) sees the
real shape instead of an opaque object — `resolve_lookup_meta` below builds
these with `json!`, so nothing constructs this type at runtime.

exists.description: Whether the referenced record row still exists at all.

is_active.description: Whether it exists *and* is live (not soft-deleted/deactivated).

name.description: The target's `primary_name_attribute` value, when it declares one.

ManifestEntry.description:
One named bundle's currently-applied state — the highest-version
`succeeded` ledger row for that name.

MatchField.description: One field of a match rule (`match_rule.fields`).

default_country.description:
A15-T3: `phone` only — the country a local number (leading `0`)
belongs to: `SA` or its calling code `966`.

is_blocking_key.description:
The sweep first narrows the peers to rows that agree on this field
(record-linkage blocking); absent on rules saved before it existed.

min_similarity.description:
`trigram` only — the `pg_trgm` similarity floor a pair must clear to
count as a match on this field (0.3 when absent).

last_scan_at.description: A15-T6: when the last full scan finished.

on_save.description:
A15-T4: what saving a likely duplicate does: `off`, `warn`,
`allow_with_reason` or `block`.

scan_schedule.description: A15-T6: `hourly`, `daily` or `weekly`; `null`: scans run only on demand.

MatchScanStarted.description: A15-T6: whether a scan was queued (`false`: one is queued already).

description.description: The server's own description: untrusted, shown as written.

text.description: The text that mentions people, with `@[user:<id>]` / `@[team:<id>]`.

skipped.description:
People mentioned (directly or through a team) who may not read the
record, or are inactive, and were not notified.

MenuItemUsage.description: One menu item's use over the period.

unused.description: Not opened in the period: a candidate to hide.

MenuView.description: A menu as one caller sees it (A21-T2).

landing.description: `<group>/<item>` of this caller's landing page, when the menu sets one.

canonical_id.description:
Which of the candidate's two records survives — must equal this
candidate's `record_a` or `record_b`. The other becomes the
duplicate and is soft-deleted, same as the ordinary
`/{entity}/{id}/merge` endpoint this delegates to.

MergeMove.description: One relationship a merge would move rows along.

MergePreview.description: A15-T5: what merging would do, without doing it.

conflicts.description: Fields a `manual` survivorship rule leaves to a person.

flows.description:
The flows an update of the survivor or a delete of the merged record
would start.

moved.description: Rows that would move from the merged record to the survivor.

result.description: The survivor's values after the merge.

merge_log_id.description: A15-T5: the merge log row; undoing the merge names it.

survivorship_conflicts.description:
Field names a `manual`-strategy survivorship rule could not
auto-decide (both records carried a non-null, differing value) — the
canonical record's pre-merge value was kept; a steward should review.
Always empty for an entity with no survivorship rules configured.

MergeResponse.description:
D-432 / M13 — the merge endpoint's response. `#[serde(flatten)]` keeps
every field an existing caller already reads (`id`, `data`, `row_version`,
…) at the top level, unchanged — `survivorship_conflicts` is purely
additive alongside them (guidelines §12: prefer additive public API
changes).

into.description: The shared tag to merge into.

rows_moved_back.description: Rows moved back to the merged records.

citations.description:
On a turn's final assistant message: the citations of the turn's
executed knowledge actions, never anything parsed from `content`
(row A-56). Empty on every other message.

oneOf.description:
C10-B: the caller's current vote on a turn's answer, `null` when there
is none (and on every other message).
On a turn's final assistant message only; `null` elsewhere.

model_id.description:
Provenance: the model and prompt version that wrote an assistant
message. `null` on user and tool messages.

terminal_state.description:
Set on a turn's final assistant message: one of the twelve terminal
states.

lineage_entities.description:
Entities this metric's query touches, when `source_kind = "query"` —
empty for manual/formula metrics or a query with no declared mapping.

children.description:
`no_recursion`: the node is recursive, and without it building the
OpenAPI document expands it inline forever (same fix as
`attome_dashboard::layout::SnapshotSection`).

cycle.description: This metric already appears higher up the tree; it is not expanded again.

metric_id.description: `None` for a formula reference to a key no active metric carries.

missing.description: A formula reference that names no active metric.

oneOf.description: The latest snapshot for the lineage period; `null` when none exists.

truncated.description: The depth limit stopped the walk here.

weight.description: A child's weight in its parent.

MetricPoint.description: One point: the bucket's start and the average of the samples in it.

admin_missing_phishing_resistant.description: An administrator with no phishing-resistant factor (a passkey).

factors.description:
`totp`, `recovery` (unused recovery codes left); `passkey` when
passkeys exist.

roles.description: The names of the account's roles.

role.description: The role's name; absent for accounts with no role.

MigrationRunDetail.description:
One run's full detail: the linked staged import's live status/counts
(D-433's "read live, never duplicated" rule) plus its
`migration_run_item` rollback ledger — this doubles as the "bundle
diff"-style surface the master plan calls for on the record side: the
same `validation_report` a caller already saw from `staged_import`'s own
response, still inspectable after the fact.

ModelFile.description: One object as a readable text file (Y1-T10).

text.description: Pretty JSON with sorted keys and a trailing newline.

ModelFiles.description:
A set of object files. Not a paginated list: an export is one artefact,
written to a directory whole and read back whole.

warnings.description:
Reasons to look again that did not stop the publish, such as an eval
suite whose score fell (N23-T2). Empty when there are none.

ModelSummary.description:
The `/api/v1/admin/predict/models*` wire shape — deliberately omits
`model_artifact` (internal fitted parameters, not a public contract) and
`organization_ref`/`row_version`/`is_deleted` (no client needs them yet).

projects.description: D-778: one section per installed vertical (project), with its areas.

licensed.description:
Always true since D-778 (no licence is checked); kept so the wire
shape stays additive (D-678).

MoveBody.description: Move a run to another version of its flow.

MoveMapping.description: One waiting step and where it lands in the target version.

found.description: The node exists in the target version with the same type.

MovePreview.description: What moving a record (with everything under it) would do.

allowed.description: Whether the move would be accepted.

moving.description: The record and its descendants: every record that moves.

refusal.description:
Why not, when it would be refused: `cycle` (the new parent is the
record or under it) or `too_deep` (the tree would pass the depth cap).

Movements.description: How the recurring revenue moved between two days, in one currency.

MyWorkAction.description:
One authoritative action a caller may take on a [`MyWorkItem`] — never
business logic of its own, only a pointer to the route that already owns
it. Dashboard (or any other caller) invokes `route` directly; the
provider never evaluates the action, only names it (the plan's "Dashboard
implements no business rule").

key.description:
Stable key for the action, e.g. `"approve"`, `"reject"` — not
displayed directly.

method.description: HTTP method the action's route expects.

route.description:
The authoritative route, with the item's own ids already substituted
(e.g. `/api/v1/approvals/{id}/decide`) — never a template the caller
has to fill in.

MyWorkItem.description: One actionable work item, from whichever provider owns it.

actions.description:
Resolved once, at list time, under this same visibility rule —
`actions()` re-resolves them fresh at click time, since eligibility
can change between the two (the plan's "checked at list time and
again at action time").

priority.description:
Free-form, provider-defined (`"high"`/`"1"`/...) — Dashboard does not
interpret it beyond display.

provider.description:
The provider's own `name()` — lets a caller group/filter without a
second lookup. Owned, not `&'static str`: `#[derive(Deserialize)]`
cannot prove a borrowed field outlives an arbitrary deserializer
lifetime, and every construction site already has a `&'static str`
literal to hand, so `.to_string()` there costs nothing that matters.

row_version.description:
The optimistic-concurrency version the item's `actions` routes expect
back, when they take one — for an approval that is the approval
request's current `row_version`, which `POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/
decide` requires. Omitted (`None`) by every provider whose actions
need no version.

source_entity.description:
The owning entity's logical name, for a client that wants to link to
the record or run its own further checks.

state.description: The record's own state/status label, for display only.

MyWorkPage.description:
A page of [`MyWorkItem`]s in the platform's keyset envelope
([`CursorPage`]): `next_cursor` is omitted on the last page.

NewDashboardFields.description:
The scalar `attome_dashboard` fields a `create_from_layout` caller supplies
— deliberately narrower than the full column set `lifecycle.rs`'s
`DashboardFieldsRow` snapshots (no `organization_id`/`thumbnail`/
`settings`/`is_template`/`template_category`/`template_version`): those
are either operator-scoped concerns an authoring caller has no basis to
set, or edited afterward through ordinary generic entity CRUD once the
dashboard exists.

credential.description: A bearer token; stored encrypted, never returned.

NewPageBody.description:
The page fields a caller may set when adding a page. `dashboard_id` is not
accepted — it always comes from the path — and neither are sections, which
the page gets exactly one of (D-527).

is_enabled.description: Defaults to false: a new portal serves nothing until it is enabled.

owning_team_ref.description: The staff team that owns records portal users create (D-576 item 7).

NewPortalUser.description: D-777: at least one of `email` and `username`.

action_id.description: A write action id, such as `record.update`.

entity.description: One entity's logical name; omit for every entity.

input.description:
The node's input and output; absent for a large pair kept in object
storage (`payload_ref`) or a node that has not run.

payload_ref.description: The object-storage key of a large input/output pair.

round.description: M3-T1: the loop round (0 outside a loop).

NotComputableResponse.description:
Phase 2/3 route stubs (`/bottlenecks`, `/conformance`, `/findings`) —
mirrors the `not_computable` shape `attome-dashboard::scenario`'s
formula-backed-metric result already uses for "the mechanism this needs
is not implemented in this workspace yet", but as a standalone 501
response rather than a written row, since these routes have nothing to
persist. See `document/module-master-plans/M41-process-intelligence.md`
§6 Phase 2/3 for what each of these will actually compute.

row_version.description: Send it back on the next PUT of this (category, channel).

The stored row's `row_version`; omit (or 0) for a (category, channel)
that has no row yet. A mismatch is a 409.

NotificationPreferences.description:
The caller's preferences: what can be muted, and what is.

A settings document rather than a `PaginatedResponse`: it is bounded by
categories × channels and read whole by the one screen that edits it,
the same shape as `GET /api/v1/settings/me`.

categories.description:
Categories the caller may mute: active, non-mandatory template keys
plus platform event names. Mandatory templates are not listed.

items.description: The caller's stored rows. A (category, channel) with no row is enabled.

agent.description: The agent object the session runs as.

code.description: The account's TOTP or recovery code, when it has MFA enabled.

OidcProviderInfo.description:
P2.8 step 5 — public provider directory for the Angular login page's
button list. Only `key`/`display_name` leave the process; `issuer`/
`client_id`/`client_secret`/`scopes`/`email_claim` are never serialized
here (`client_secret` in particular must never reach a GET response).

OnTimeout.description:
What happens when a step's `sla_minutes` elapses with nobody having
decided it yet — applied by `apply_step_timeout_with`, driven by the sweep
that reuses M51's notification-escalation poller
(`xrm_notification::poller`; see that crate's `approval_timeouts` module).

name.description: Kebab-case, at most 60 characters; becomes the file name.

requires.description:
`{ platform?: ">=X.Y.Z", after?: ["<layer>/<scope>/<NNNN>-<name>"],
modules?: [module key] }`; `platform` defaults to this binary.

scope.description:
Lowercase letters and digits joined by `-` or `_`; `platform` for a
platform changeset.

OpsNode.description: One node, from its heartbeat in the metrics store.

healthy.description: It stored its metrics in the last three minutes.

to_user.description: Who decides your approvals while you are away.

ended.description: How many current or future out-of-office delegations were ended.

widgets.description: One entry per widget on the page, in layout order.

publish_at.description:
M56 Phase 1 (D-436, migration `0230`) — when set on a `draft` page,
the scheduled-publish sweep publishes it once `NOW()` passes this.

review_by.description:
M37 Phase 2 (D-452) — when set, the owner (`updated_by`) is reminded
through M51 once `NOW()` passes it, and retrieval callers are told the
underlying content is stale. `None` means no review cadence is set,
not "never review".

template_id.description: `None` if this page was built from scratch, not from a template.

unpublish_at.description:
When set on a `published` page, the same sweep reverts it to `draft`
once `NOW()` passes this.

PageStats.description:
The read model `attome_content::analytics::rollup_page_stats` maintains
(D-452). Served by the admin page-stats panel; not written directly by
any request handler.

PaginatedResponse_AccessReviewCampaign.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

scope_entity_id.description:
`entity_info.id` (real FK — see this module's doc comment),
not the entity's logicalname; resolve via the entities admin API for
display.

PaginatedResponse_AccessReviewItem.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

PaginatedResponse_ActiveBan.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

items.description: Q20-T5: one active temporary ban.

category.description: The limit category that tripped last.

PaginatedResponse_AgentCard.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

items.description: One agent a partner can hand work to.

PaginatedResponse_ApiKeyMeta.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

PaginatedResponse_ApiUsageSummaryRow.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

PaginatedResponse_AppDetail.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this app: `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer
may update or retire it (409 `layer_mismatch` otherwise).

PaginatedResponse_ApprovalPolicyView.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

condition.description:
M45 expression string, evaluated per-invocation against the gated
action's payload (`attome_audit::approval::condition_permits`) — see
that function's doc comment for the fail-closed semantics.

PaginatedResponse_ApprovalRequestView.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page.

oneOf.description:
D-421 — `Some` only for a request a policy (or a workflow approval
node consulting one) supplied a multi-step plan for; `None` means
this request still runs the original flat `required_approvals`
model, decided via `POST .../decide` exactly as before.

items.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/resources/capacity` — a single resource's
capacity/demand picture over the requested `[from, to]` period (M72).
See `capacity.rs`'s module doc for the exact arithmetic behind each
field — in short: `capacity_hours` is the platform's default business
calendar over the period, net of approved leave; `allocated_hours` is
`resource_allocation.allocation_percent` prorated by date overlap;
`actual_hours` is `project_time_entry.hours`, unrelated to either.

actual_hours.description:
`SUM(hours)` from `project_time_entry` for this resource, entries
dated within `[from, to]` — what was actually logged, independent of
what was planned.

allocated_hours.description:
`SUM(allocation_percent / 100 * capacity_hours * overlap_days /
period_days)` across every `resource_allocation` row overlapping
the period — prorated against the period's nominal (pre-leave)
capacity, not the leave-adjusted figure above; see `capacity.rs`.

capacity_hours.description:
Business-calendar working hours over `[from, to]`, net of any
`resource_availability` leave overlapping the period.

over_allocated.description:
`allocated_hours > capacity_hours` — the resource is committed past
what the period's business calendar (net of leave) can deliver.

resource_name.description:
`user_account.user_name` — `None` for a legacy row with no
username set, same optionality the column itself carries.

utilization_pct.description:
`allocated_hours / capacity_hours * 100`; `0.0` when `capacity_hours`
is `0` (e.g. a period with no working days at all, or a resource on
leave for the whole period) rather than a division-by-zero `NaN`.

items.description: One record of any entity. P-api-contract Phase 1: the platform dispatches generic CRUD from runtime metadata (D-003), so `data`'s property names differ per entity and per deployment and cannot be enumerated in a static document — call `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields. Everything outside `data` is the same on every entity.

approval_request_id.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): present only on the response to an update that
asked for a state transition requiring approval. The record was moved
to the transition's pending state (visible in `data`) instead of the
requested one, and this is the approval request that decides it
(`/api/v1/approvals/{id}/decide`). Omitted on every other response, so
those stay byte-identical.

created_at.description:
UTC ISO-8601. Typed `Value` in Rust because it is read straight out of
the dynamic row, but it is always a timestamp string or `null`.

data.description:
The record's own columns, keyed by attribute logical name. Values are
whatever the attribute's field type maps to in JSON.

duplicate_warnings.description:
A15-T4: the existing records this create or update matches under a
`warn` (or reasoned `allow_with_reason`) duplicate rule — the write
succeeded. Omitted when there are none.

expanded.description:
S1-T4: with `?expand=`, the records the named lookups point at, keyed
by lookup attribute; a target the caller may not read is absent.

hidden_duplicates.description: A15-T4: how many more matches the caller may not read. Omitted when 0.

lookups.description:
P-entity-contract-hardening item (a) â€” supersedes D-057's read-time
nulling (DECISIONS.md). `data` always carries the stored UUID for a
lookup field, unmodified; this sibling map carries the tombstone
metadata a client needs instead of a fabricated `null`. `None` (and
therefore omitted from the JSON body â€” `skip_serializing_if`) for any
entity with no populated lookup fields, so a non-lookup entity's
response is byte-identical to before this field existed.

merged_into.description:
A15-T5: this record was merged into that one (the entity keeps merged
records); omitted otherwise.

warnings.description:
D-791 rule 6: the `warning`-severity business-rule `error` policies
that fired on this create, update or upsert — the write succeeded;
the form shows them. Omitted when there are none (and on reads), so
every other response stays byte-identical.
